translations.literal: State and grain altars; morning sun and evening moon; former agriculture; former silkworms; high altars of procreation; sacrificial announcements; prayer and report; spirits; stars—Spirit Star, Longevity Star, Director of the Center, Director of Fate, Director of the People, Director of Salary; Great Year, monthly generals, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain; peaks, garrisons, seas, rivers, mountains and streams; city god

sentences.zh: ○社稷

translations.literal: ● State and grain altars
translations.idiomatic: State and Grain Altars

sentences.zh: 社稷之祀，自京師以及王國府州縣皆有之。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to the state and grain altars existed from the capital through princely states, prefectures, and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices to the state and grain altars were performed from the capital down through princely domains, prefectures, and counties.

sentences.zh: 其壇在宮城西南者，曰太社稷。

translations.literal: The altar southwest of the palace city was called the Grand State and Grain Altars.
translations.idiomatic: The altar in the southwest of the palace precinct was known as the Grand State and Grain Altars.

sentences.zh: 明初建太社在東，太稷在西，壇皆北向。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming, the Grand State altar was built in the east and the Grand Grain altar in the west; both altars faced north.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Ming, the Grand State altar stood in the east and the Grand Grain altar in the west, with both platforms facing north.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，中書省臣定議：「周制，小宗伯掌建國之神位，右社稷，左宗廟。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 1, Secretariat ministers resolved: "Under Zhou institutions, the junior Director of Ancestral Rites supervised the spirit tablets of the founding of the state, placing the state and grain altars on the right and the ancestral temples on the left.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongwu, ministers of the Secretariat resolved: "Under Zhou ritual, the junior Director of Ancestral Rites set the spirit seats of state founding, with the state and grain altars on the right and the ancestral temples on the left.

sentences.zh: 社稷之祀，壇而不屋。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to the state and grain was performed at altars, not in buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings to state and grain were made at open altars, not within roofed halls.

sentences.zh: 其制在中門之外，外門之內。

translations.literal: Their arrangement lay outside the central gate and inside the outer gate.
translations.idiomatic: They were positioned outside the central gate but within the outer gate.

sentences.zh: 尊而親之，與先祖等。

translations.literal: They were honored with intimacy, equal to ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: They were revered with the same intimacy accorded to forebears.

sentences.zh: 然天子有三社。

translations.literal: Yet the Son of Heaven had three state altars.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Son of Heaven maintained three state altars.

sentences.zh: 爲羣姓立者曰太社。

translations.literal: That established for all clans was called the Grand State Altar.
translations.idiomatic: The altar erected on behalf of all clans was called the Grand State Altar.

sentences.zh: 其自爲立者曰王社。

translations.literal: That which he established for himself was called the Royal State Altar.
translations.idiomatic: The one he established for himself was called the Royal State Altar.

sentences.zh: 又勝國之社屋之，國雖亡而存之，以重神也。

translations.literal: Further, the conquered state's altar was roofed; though the state perished, it was preserved to give weight to the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The altar of a conquered state was given a roof; though the realm had fallen, the shrine was kept standing to honor the spirit.

sentences.zh: 後世天子惟立太社、太稷。

translations.literal: In later ages the Son of Heaven established only the Grand State and Grand Grain altars.
translations.idiomatic: In later periods, the Son of Heaven established only the Grand State and Grand Grain altars.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖立官太社、太稷，一歲各再祀。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han established the ministerial Grand State and Grand Grain altars, each sacrificed to twice a year.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han founded the ministerial Grand State and Grand Grain altars, each receiving two sacrifices per year.

sentences.zh: 光武立太社稷於洛陽宗廟之右，春秋二仲月及臘，一歲三祀。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu established the Grand State and Grain at Luoyang to the right of the ancestral temples, sacrificing in the second months of spring and autumn and at the La festival—three times a year.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu placed the Grand State and Grain altars to the right of the ancestral temples at Luoyang, with offerings in the mid-spring and mid-autumn months and at the La festival—three times yearly.

sentences.zh: 唐因隋制，並建社稷於含光門右，仲春、秋戊日祭之。

translations.literal: Tang followed Sui institutions, building both altars to the right of Hanguang Gate, sacrificing on the wu days of mid-spring and mid-autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang followed Sui practice, erecting both altars to the right of Hanguang Gate and sacrificing on the wu days of mid-spring and mid-autumn.

sentences.zh: 玄宗升社稷爲大祀，仍令四時致祭。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong elevated state and grain to the rank of great sacrifice and still ordered offerings in all four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong raised the state and grain rites to great-sacrifice status and ordered offerings in all four seasons.

sentences.zh: 宋制如東漢時。

translations.literal: Song institutions followed the Eastern Han period.
translations.idiomatic: Song ritual followed the Eastern Han model.

sentences.zh: 元世祖營社稷於和義門內，以春秋二仲上戊日祭。

translations.literal: Kublai Khan built the state and grain altars within Heyi Gate, sacrificing on the upper wu days of mid-spring and mid-autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai Khan established the altars within Heyi Gate, with sacrifices on the upper wu days of mid-spring and mid-autumn.

sentences.zh: 今宜祀以春秋二仲月上戊日。

translations.literal: Now sacrifices should be performed on the upper wu days of the second months of spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices should now be held on the upper wu days of mid-spring and mid-autumn.

sentences.zh: 」是年二月，太祖親祀太社、太稷。

translations.literal: " In the second month of that year the Founding Emperor personally sacrificed to the Grand State and Grand Grain.
translations.idiomatic: " That year in the second month, the Founding Emperor personally offered sacrifice to the Grand State and Grand Grain altars.

sentences.zh: 社配以后土，西向。

translations.literal: The state altar was matched with Queen Earth, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Queen Earth was paired with the state altar, facing west.

sentences.zh: 稷配以後稷，東向。

translations.literal: The grain altar was matched with Hou Ji, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ji was paired with the grain altar, facing east.

sentences.zh: 帝服皮弁服，省牲；

translations.literal: The Emperor wore the skin cap and robes and inspected the sacrificial animals;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore court ritual dress and inspected the victims;

sentences.zh: 通天冠、絳紗袍，行三獻禮。

translations.literal: wearing the communication-with-Heaven cap and crimson gauze robe, he performed the three-offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: then, in the communication-with-Heaven cap and crimson gauze robe, conducted the threefold offering rite.

sentences.zh: 初，帝命中書省翰林院議創屋，備風雨。

translations.literal: Initially the Emperor ordered the Secretariat and Hanlin Academy to discuss building halls to shelter from wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor directed the Secretariat and Hanlin Academy to consider erecting halls against wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 學士陶安言：「天子太社必受風雨霜露。

translations.literal: Academician Tao An said: "The Son of Heaven's Grand State Altar must receive wind, rain, frost, and dew.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Tao An argued: "The Son of Heaven's Grand State altar must be exposed to wind, rain, frost, and dew.

sentences.zh: 亡國之社則屋之，不受天陽也。

translations.literal: The altar of a perished state was roofed, not receiving the yang of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Only a conquered state's altar was roofed, denied the yang light of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 建屋非宜。

translations.literal: Building halls would be inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Erecting buildings would be improper.

sentences.zh: 若遇風雨，則請於齋宮望祭。

translations.literal: If wind and rain occurred, sacrifice from the fasting palace by gazing toward the altars was requested.
translations.idiomatic: In stormy weather, offerings should be made by gaze-sacrifice from the fasting palace.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 三年，於壇北建祭殿五間，又北建拜殿五間，以備風雨。

translations.literal: In year three, five bays of sacrificial hall were built north of the altar, and five more bays of bowing hall further north, to provide against wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, a five-bay sacrificial hall was built north of the altar and a five-bay bowing hall beyond it, for shelter in bad weather.

sentences.zh: 十年，太祖以社稷分祭，配祀未當，下禮官議，尚書張籌言：

translations.literal: In year ten, the Founding Emperor held that separate sacrifice to state and grain with improper matched spirits was wrong; he ordered ritual officials to deliberate, and Minister Zhang Chou said:
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, finding separate state and grain sacrifices with unsuitable spirit pairings, the Founding Emperor referred the matter to ritual officials; Minister Zhang Chou argued:

sentences.zh: 按《通典》，顓頊祀共工氏子句龍爲后土。

translations.literal: According to the Tongdian, Zhuanxu sacrificed Gong Gong's son Gou Long as Queen Earth.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Tongdian, Zhuanxu sacrificed Gong Gong's son Gou Long as Queen Earth.

sentences.zh: 后土，社也。

translations.literal: Queen Earth is the state altar.
translations.idiomatic: Queen Earth is the state altar.

sentences.zh: 烈山氏子柱爲稷。

translations.literal: The son of the Flame Emperor, Zhu, was made grain lord.
translations.idiomatic: The Flame Emperor's son Zhu was appointed grain lord.

sentences.zh: 稷，田正也。

translations.literal: Grain lord is the director of the fields.
translations.idiomatic: The grain lord was director of the fields.

sentences.zh: 唐、虞、夏因之。

translations.literal: Tang, Yu, and Xia followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang, Yu, and Xia dynasties followed this practice.

sentences.zh: 此社稷所由始也。

translations.literal: This was the origin of the state and grain altars.
translations.idiomatic: This was how the state and grain altars originated.

sentences.zh: 商湯因旱遷社，以後稷代柱。

translations.literal: King Tang of Shang, because of drought, moved the state altar and replaced Zhu with Hou Ji.
translations.idiomatic: King Tang of Shang, during drought, moved the state altar and replaced Zhu with Hou Ji.

sentences.zh: 欲遷句龍，無可繼者，故止。

translations.literal: He wished to move Gou Long but had no successor, and therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to displace Gou Long but found no successor, and so desisted.

sentences.zh: 然王肅謂社祭句龍，稷祭后稷，皆人鬼，非地祇。

translations.literal: Yet Wang Su held that the state altar sacrificed to Gou Long and the grain altar to Hou Ji—both human ghosts, not earthly spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Su held that the state altar honored Gou Long and the grain altar Hou Ji—both human spirits, not earthly deities.

sentences.zh: 而陳氏《禮書》又謂社祭五土之祇，稷祭五穀之神。

translations.literal: Chen's Book of Rites further held that the state altar sacrificed to the spirits of the five soils and the grain altar to the spirits of the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's Book of Rites further held that the state altar honored the spirits of the five soils and the grain altar the spirits of the five grains.

sentences.zh: 鄭康成亦謂社爲五土總神，稷爲原隰之神。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan also held that the state altar was the general spirit of the five soils and the grain altar the spirit of lowlands and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan likewise held that the state altar was the general deity of the five soils and the grain altar the deity of lowlands and marshes.

sentences.zh: 句龍有平水土功，故配社，后稷有播種功，故配稷。

translations.literal: Gou Long had the merit of leveling water and soil and therefore was matched with the state altar; Hou Ji had the merit of sowing seed and therefore was matched with the grain altar.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gou Long had leveled water and soil, he was paired with the state altar; because Hou Ji had spread seed, he was paired with the grain altar.

sentences.zh: 二說不同。

translations.literal: The two theories differ.
translations.idiomatic: The two interpretations diverged.

sentences.zh: 漢元始中，以夏禹配官社，后稷配官稷。

translations.literal: In the Yuanshi era of Han, Yu the Great was matched with the ministerial state altar and Hou Ji with the ministerial grain altar.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanshi period of Han, Yu the Great was paired with the ministerial state altar and Hou Ji with the ministerial grain altar.

sentences.zh: 唐、宋及元又以句龍配社，周棄配稷。

translations.literal: Tang, Song, and Yuan again matched Gou Long with the state altar and Zhou Qi with the grain altar.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang, Song, and Yuan, Gou Long was again paired with the state altar and Zhou Qi with the grain altar.

sentences.zh: 此配祀之制，初無定論也。

translations.literal: This system of matched spirits had no settled conclusion from the start.
translations.idiomatic: From the outset, no settled consensus governed these spirit pairings.

sentences.zh: 至社稷分合之義，《書召誥》言『社於新邑」，孔注曰：「社稷共牢。

translations.literal: As for the meaning of combining and separating state and grain, the Announcement of Duke Shao says "establish the state altar at the new city," and Kong's commentary states: "State and grain shared one pen.
translations.idiomatic: On whether state and grain should be combined or separated, the Announcement of Duke Shao says "establish the state altar at the new city," and Kong's commentary reads: "State and grain shared one pen.

sentences.zh: 」《周禮》「封人掌設王之社壝」，注云：「不言稷者，舉社則稷從之。

translations.literal: " The Rites of Zhou states "the border officer supervises setting the king's state altar mound," with a note: "Grain is not mentioned; when state is mentioned, grain follows.
translations.idiomatic: " The Rites of Zhou states that "the border officer supervises setting the king's state altar mound," with a note: "Grain is not mentioned; when state is mentioned, grain follows.

sentences.zh: 」陳氏《禮書》曰：「稷非土無以生，土非稷無以見生生之效，故祭社必及稷。

translations.literal: " Chen's Book of Rites says: "Grain cannot live without soil, and soil cannot show the effect of sustaining life without grain; therefore in sacrificing to the state altar grain must be included.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen's Book of Rites says: "Grain cannot live without soil, and soil cannot display the power of sustaining life without grain; therefore sacrifice to the state altar must include grain.

sentences.zh: 」《山堂考索》曰：「社爲九土之尊，稷爲五穀之長，稷生於土，則社與稷固不可分。

translations.literal: " The Shantang Kaosuo says: "The state altar is the honor of the nine soils; grain is the chief of the five grains; grain grows from soil—state and grain therefore cannot be separated.
translations.idiomatic: " The Shantang Kaosuo says: "The state altar is supreme among the nine soils; grain is chief among the five grains; grain grows from soil—state and grain therefore cannot be divided.

sentences.zh: 」其宜合祭，古有明證。

translations.literal: " Their proper joint sacrifice has clear proof in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: " That they should be sacrificed together has clear ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 請社稷共爲一罈。

translations.literal: It is requested that state and grain share one altar mound.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that state and grain share a single altar mound.

sentences.zh: 至句龍，共工氏之子也，祀之無義。

translations.literal: As for Gou Long, son of the Gong Gong clan, sacrificing to him has no justification.
translations.idiomatic: As for Gou Long, a son of the Gong Gong line, honoring him lacked justification.

sentences.zh: 商湯欲遷未果。

translations.literal: King Tang of Shang wished to move him but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: King Tang of Shang had wished to remove him but could not.

sentences.zh: 漢嘗易以夏禹，而夏禹今已列祀帝王之次，棄稷亦配先農。

translations.literal: Han once replaced him with Yu the Great, but Yu the Great now already ranks among the sacrifices to emperors, and Qi of Zhou is also matched at the Former Agriculture altar.
translations.idiomatic: Han once substituted Yu the Great, but Yu the Great now already receives sacrifice among the emperors, and Qi of Zhou is also paired at the Former Agriculture altar.

sentences.zh: 請罷句龍、棄配位，謹奉仁祖淳皇帝配享，以成一代盛典。

translations.literal: It is requested to remove the matched seats of Gou Long and Qi, and respectfully to offer the Pure Emperor Renzu as matched spirit, to complete a ritual worthy of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Gou Long and Qi be removed from their paired seats and that the Pure Emperor Renzu be installed as matched spirit, to complete a ritual worthy of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 遂改作於午門之右，社稷共爲一罈。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was rebuilt to the right of the Meridian Gate, state and grain sharing one altar mound.
translations.idiomatic: The altars were then rebuilt to the right of the Meridian Gate, with state and grain sharing one mound.

sentences.zh: 初，社稷列中祀，及以仁祖配，乃升爲上祀。

translations.literal: Initially state and grain were ranked as middle sacrifices; when the Pure Emperor was made matched spirit, they were elevated to upper sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: State and grain had initially ranked as middle sacrifices; once the Pure Emperor was made matched spirit, they were raised to upper sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 具冕服以祭，行奉安禮。

translations.literal: Full ritual robes were provided for sacrifice, and the enshrinement rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: Full ritual vestments were used, and the enshrinement rite was performed.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，祭社稷行新定儀。

translations.literal: In the spring of year eleven, state and grain were sacrificed to under the newly fixed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year, the state and grain rites followed the newly fixed protocol.

sentences.zh: 迎神、飲福、送神凡十二拜，餘如舊。

translations.literal: Welcoming the spirit, drinking the blessing, and sending off the spirit totaled twelve bows; the rest followed the old.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the spirit, drinking the blessing, and sending off the spirit required twelve bows in all; the remainder followed former practice.

sentences.zh: 建文時，更奉太祖配，永樂中。

translations.literal: In the Jianwen period the Founding Emperor was again made matched spirit; in the Yongle period,
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwen reign the Founding Emperor was again made matched spirit; under Yongle,

sentences.zh: 北京社稷壇成，制如南京。

translations.literal: the Beijing state and grain altar was completed, with regulations like those of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: the Beijing state and grain altar was completed, following the Nanjing model.

sentences.zh: 洪熙後，奉太祖、太宗同配。

translations.literal: After the Hongxi reign, the Founding Emperor and the Martial Emperor were jointly matched.
translations.idiomatic: After Hongxi, the Founding Emperor and the Martial Emperor were jointly paired.

sentences.zh: 舊制，上丁釋奠孔子，次日上戊祀社稷。

translations.literal: Under the old system, on the upper si day the libation to Confucius was performed, and on the next day the upper wu day sacrifice to state and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Under the former rule, the Confucian libation fell on the upper si day, and the state and grain sacrifice on the following upper wu day.

sentences.zh: 弘治十七年八月，上丁在初十日，上戊在朔日，禮官請以十一日祀社稷。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Hongzhi 17, the upper si fell on the tenth day and the upper wu on the first day of the month; ritual officials requested sacrifice to state and grain on the eleventh.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Hongzhi 17, the upper si day fell on the tenth and the upper wu on the first of the month; ritual officials asked to move the state and grain sacrifice to the eleventh.

sentences.zh: 御史金洪劾之，言如此則中戊，非上戊矣。

translations.literal: Censor Jin Hong impeached this, saying that in that case it would be the middle wu, not the upper wu.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jin Hong objected that this would make it the middle wu day, not the upper wu.

sentences.zh: 禮部覆奏言：「洪武二十年嘗以十一日爲上戊，失不始今日。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites replied in memorial: "In Hongwu 20 the eleventh day was once taken as upper wu—the error did not begin today.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites replied: "In Hongwu 20 the eleventh was once treated as upper wu—the lapse did not begin only now.

sentences.zh: 」命遵舊制，仍用上戊。

translations.literal: " An order followed the old system, still using the upper wu.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered the former rule kept, still using the upper wu day.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年諭禮部：「天地至尊，次則宗廟，又次則社稷。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 9 the emperor instructed the Ministry of Rites: "Heaven and Earth are supreme; next come the ancestral temples; next again state and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9 the emperor instructed the Ministry of Rites: "Heaven and Earth are supreme; next the ancestral temples; and next the state and grain altars.

sentences.zh: 今奉祖配天，又奉祖配社，此禮官之失也。

translations.literal: Now the ancestor is matched with Heaven and again matched with the state altar—this is the ritual officials' error.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial ancestor is paired with Heaven and again with the state altar—this is the ritual officials' mistake.

sentences.zh: 宜改從皇祖舊制，太社以句龍配，太稷以後稷配。

translations.literal: The former system of the imperial ancestor should be restored: the Grand State Altar should be matched with Gou Long and the Grand Grain Altar with Hou Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral practice should be restored: Gou Long should pair with the Grand State Altar and Hou Ji with the Grand Grain Altar.

sentences.zh: 」乃以更正社稷壇配位禮，告太廟及社稷，遂藏二配位於寢廟，更定行八拜禮。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the ritual of correcting the matched spirits at the state and grain altar was performed, announced to the Grand Ancestral Temple and to state and grain; the two matched tablets were stored in the resting temple, and the eight-bow rite was newly fixed.
translations.idiomatic: " The rite correcting the altar pairings was announced to the Grand Ancestral Temple and to state and grain; the two paired tablets were stored in the resting temple, and the eight-bow rite was newly established.

sentences.zh: 其壇在西苑豳風亭之西者，曰帝社稷。

translations.literal: The altar west of the Binfeng Pavilion in the Western Park was called the Imperial State and Grain Altars.
translations.idiomatic: The altar west of the Binfeng Pavilion in the Western Park was called the Imperial State and Grain Altars.

sentences.zh: 東帝社，西帝稷，皆北向。

translations.literal: Imperial State in the east and Imperial Grain in the west, both facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial State altar stood in the east and the Imperial Grain in the west, both facing north.

sentences.zh: 始名西苑土谷壇。

translations.literal: It was first named the Western Park Soil and Grain Altar.
translations.idiomatic: It was first named the Western Park Soil and Grain Altar.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年，帝謂土谷壇亦社稷耳，何以別於太社稷？

translations.literal: In Jiajing 10 the emperor said the Soil and Grain Altar is also state and grain—why distinguish it from the Grand State and Grain?
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 10 the emperor remarked that the Soil and Grain Altar was itself state and grain—why should it differ from the Grand State and Grain?

sentences.zh: 張璁等言： 「古者天子稱王，今若稱王社、王稷，與王府社稷名同。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong and others said: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven was called king; if now it were called Royal State and Royal Grain, the names would be the same as princely state and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and others replied: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven was styled king; to call them Royal State and Royal Grain would duplicate princely nomenclature.

sentences.zh: 前定神牌曰五土谷之神，名義至當。

translations.literal: The earlier fixed spirit tablet reading Spirit of the Five Soils and Grains is most apt in name and meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier spirit tablet, Spirit of the Five Soils and Grains, was most fitting in name and meaning.

sentences.zh: 」帝採帝耤之義，改爲帝社、帝稷，以上戊明日祭。

translations.literal: " The emperor adopted the meaning of the Imperial Plough and changed them to Imperial State and Imperial Grain, sacrificing on the day after the upper wu.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took the meaning of the Imperial Plough field and renamed them Imperial State and Imperial Grain, sacrificing on the day after the upper wu.

sentences.zh: 後改次戊，次戊在望後，則仍用上巳。

translations.literal: Later it was changed to the second wu; when the second wu fell after the full moon, the upper si was still used.
translations.idiomatic: Later the date shifted to the second wu; when the second wu fell after the full moon, the upper si was used instead.

sentences.zh: 春告秋報爲定制。

translations.literal: Spring announcement and autumn report became the fixed custom.
translations.idiomatic: Spring announcement and autumn report became fixed practice.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，禮部言：「帝社稷之名，自古所無，嫌於煩數，宜罷。

translations.literal: In Longqing 1 the Ministry of Rites said: "The name Imperial State and Grain has never existed in antiquity and seems unduly elaborate—it should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 1 the Ministry of Rites argued: "The title Imperial State and Grain is unknown in antiquity and seems unduly elaborate—it should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 中都亦有太社壇，洪武四年建。

translations.literal: The Central Capital also had a Grand State altar, built in Hongwu 4.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Capital also had a Grand State altar, built in Hongwu 4.

sentences.zh: 取五方土以築。

translations.literal: Soil from the five directions was taken to build it.
translations.idiomatic: It was built with soil from the five directions.

sentences.zh: 直隸、河南進黃土，浙江、福建、廣東、廣西進赤土，江西、湖廣、陝西進白土，山東進青土，北平進黑土。

translations.literal: Zhili and Henan presented yellow soil; Zhejiang, Fujian, Guangdong, and Guangxi presented red soil; Jiangxi, Huguang, and Shaanxi presented white soil; Shandong presented green soil; Beiping presented black soil.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili and Henan sent yellow soil; Zhejiang, Fujian, Guangdong, and Guangxi red soil; Jiangxi, Huguang, and Shaanxi white soil; Shandong green soil; and Beiping black soil.

sentences.zh: 天下府縣千三百餘城，各土百斤，取於名山高爽之地。

translations.literal: From more than thirteen hundred prefectures and counties nationwide, one hundred jin of soil from each, taken from famous mountains on high, open ground.
translations.idiomatic: From more than thirteen hundred prefectures and counties nationwide, one hundred jin of soil each, taken from famous mountains on high, open ground.

sentences.zh: 王國社稷，洪武四年定。

translations.literal: Princely state state and grain altars were fixed in Hongwu 4.
translations.idiomatic: Princely state and grain altars were regulated in Hongwu 4.

sentences.zh: 十一年，禮臣言：「太社稷既同壇合祭，王國各府州縣亦宜同壇，稱國社國稷之神，不設配位。

translations.literal: In year eleven ritual officials said: "Since the Grand State and Grain now share one altar for joint sacrifice, princely states, prefectures, and counties should also share one altar, styled Spirit of the State and Grain of the Domain, with no matched spirits set.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year ritual officials argued: "Since the Grand State and Grain now share one mound, princely domains, prefectures, and counties should likewise use one altar, titled Spirit of the State and Grain of the Domain, with no paired spirits.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict approved.

sentences.zh: 十三年九月，復定制兩壇一壝如初式。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of year thirteen, the former system of two altars within one mound was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year, the former arrangement of two altars within one mound was restored.

sentences.zh: 十八年，定王國祭社稷山川等儀，行十二拜禮。

translations.literal: In year eighteen, the ritual for princely sacrifice to state and grain, mountains and streams, and the like was fixed, using a twelve-bow rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, the protocol for princely sacrifice to state and grain, mountains and streams, and the like was fixed, with a twelve-bow rite.

sentences.zh: 府州縣社稷，洪武元年頒壇制於天下郡邑，俱設於本城西北，右社左稷。

translations.literal: Prefecture and county state and grain altars: in Hongwu 1 altar regulations were issued to all commanderies and districts, all set in the northwest of the local city, state altar on the right and grain altar on the left.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1, altar regulations were issued to every prefecture and county: each was placed in the northwest of the city, with the state altar on the right and the grain altar on the left.

sentences.zh: 十一年，定同壇合祭如京師。

translations.literal: In year eleven, joint sacrifice on one altar was fixed, as at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, a single shared altar for joint sacrifice was mandated, following the capital model.

sentences.zh: 獻官以守禦武臣爲初獻，文官爲亞獻、終獻。

translations.literal: The offering official took the defending military officer as first offerer and the civil officer as second and final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: The first offering was performed by the defending military officer, with civil officials as second and final offerers.

sentences.zh: 十三年，溧水縣祭社稷，以牛醢代鹿醢。

translations.literal: In year thirteen, Lishui County sacrificed to state and grain, using beef paste in place of deer paste.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Lishui County sacrificed to state and grain, substituting beef paste for deer paste.

sentences.zh: 禮部言：「定制，祭物缺者許以他物代。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said: "Under fixed regulations, when sacrificial items are lacking, another item may be substituted.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites argued: "Under established regulations, missing sacrificial items may be replaced with others.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「所謂缺者，以非土地所產。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "What is meant by lacking is what the land does not produce.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "Lacking means what the locality cannot produce.

sentences.zh: 溧水固有鹿，是有司故爲苟簡也。

translations.literal: Lishui certainly has deer—this was the officials' deliberate negligence.
translations.idiomatic: Lishui certainly has deer—this was official negligence, not genuine shortage.

sentences.zh: 百司所以能理其職而盡民事者，以其常存敬懼之心耳。

translations.literal: That the hundred offices can manage their duties and fulfill the people's affairs rests on their constantly preserving a heart of reverence and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Officials can govern their duties and serve the people only if they keep a constant heart of reverence and awe.

sentences.zh: 神猶忽之，於人事又何懼焉！

translations.literal: If even the spirits are treated with neglect, how much less fear would there be in human affairs!
translations.idiomatic: If even the spirits are treated carelessly, what restraint would remain in human affairs!

sentences.zh: 」命論如律。

translations.literal: " An order was given to punish according to law.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered punishment according to law.

sentences.zh: 乃敕禮部下天下郡邑，凡祭祀必備物，苟非地產、無從市鬻者，聽其缺。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was sent to the Ministry of Rites to notify all commanderies and districts that in every sacrifice the full complement of items must be prepared; only what is not local produce and cannot be obtained in the market may be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Ministry of Rites to notify every prefecture and county that sacrifices must include the full prescribed offerings, allowing omissions only for items neither locally produced nor obtainable in the market.

sentences.zh: 十四年，令三獻皆以文職長官，武官不與。

translations.literal: In year fourteen, all three offerings were assigned to senior civil officials; military officers were excluded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, all three offerings were assigned to senior civil officials, excluding military officers.

sentences.zh: 里社，每裏一百戶立壇一所，祀五土五穀之神。

translations.literal: District state altars: for every district of one hundred households one altar was established, sacrificing to the spirits of the five soils and five grains.
translations.idiomatic: At the district level, one altar was established per hundred-household district, honoring the spirits of the five soils and five grains.

sentences.zh: ○朝日夕月

translations.literal: ● Morning sun and evening moon
translations.idiomatic: Morning Sun and Evening Moon

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，禮部言：

translations.literal: In Hongwu 3 the Ministry of Rites said:
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 the Ministry of Rites reported:

sentences.zh: 古者祀日月之禮有六。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were six rites for sacrificing to the sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity there were six forms of sacrifice to the sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 《郊特牲》曰：「郊之祭，大報天而主日，配以月」，一也。

translations.literal: The Suburban Sacrifice says: "In suburban sacrifice, there is great report to Heaven with the sun as chief and the moon as matched"—the first.
translations.idiomatic: The Suburban Sacrifice states: "In suburban sacrifice, there is great report to Heaven with the sun as chief and the moon as matched"—the first form.

sentences.zh: 《玉藻》曰：「翰日於東門之外」，《祭義》曰：「祭日於東郊，祭月於西郊」，二也。

translations.literal: The Jade Ornaments says: "Gaze upon the sun outside the eastern gate"; the Meaning of Sacrifice says: "Sacrifice to the sun in the eastern suburb and to the moon in the western suburb"—the second.
translations.idiomatic: The Jade Ornaments reads: "Gaze upon the sun outside the eastern gate"; the Meaning of Sacrifice says: "Sacrifice to the sun in the eastern suburb and to the moon in the western suburb"—the second.

sentences.zh: 《小宗伯》：「肆類於四郊，兆日於東郊，兆月於西郊」，三也。

translations.literal: The Junior Director of Ancestral Rites: "Perform the category sacrifice in the four suburbs, establish the sun in the eastern suburb and the moon in the western suburb"—the third.
translations.idiomatic: The Junior Director of Ancestral Rites: "Perform the category sacrifice in the four suburbs, establish the sun in the eastern suburb and the moon in the western suburb"—the third.

sentences.zh: 《月令》：孟冬「祈來年於天宗」，天宗，日月之類，四也。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances: in the first month of winter "pray for the coming year at the Heavenly Ancestor"; the Heavenly Ancestor is of the class of sun and moon—the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances: in mid-winter "pray for the coming year at the Heavenly Ancestor"; the Heavenly Ancestor belongs to the class of sun and moon—the fourth.

sentences.zh: 《覲禮》：「拜日於東門之外，反祀方明，禮日於南門之外，禮月於北門之外」，五也。

translations.literal: The Audience Rites: "Bow to the sun outside the eastern gate; on return sacrifice to the Bright Square; perform the sun rite outside the southern gate and the moon rite outside the northern gate"—the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: The Audience Rites: "Bow to the sun outside the eastern gate; on return sacrifice to the Bright Square; perform the sun rite outside the southern gate and the moon rite outside the northern gate"—the fifth.

sentences.zh: 「霜雪風雨之不時，則禜日月」，六也。

translations.literal: "When frost, snow, wind, and rain are untimely, then perform the exorcistic sacrifice to sun and moon"—the sixth.
translations.idiomatic: "When frost, snow, wind, and rain are untimely, perform the exorcistic sacrifice to sun and moon"—the sixth.

sentences.zh: 說者謂因郊祀而祀之，非正祀也。

translations.literal: Expositors hold that sacrifice along with suburban rites is not orthodox sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that sacrifice incidental to suburban rites was not orthodox sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 類禜而祀之，與覲諸侯而禮之，非常祀也。

translations.literal: Sacrifice by category and exorcism, and performing rites when receiving feudal lords, were not regular sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice by category or exorcism, and rites performed when receiving feudal lords, were extraordinary, not regular offerings.

sentences.zh: 惟春分朝之於東門外，秋分夕之於西門外者，祀之正與常也。

translations.literal: Only morning audience to the sun outside the eastern gate at the spring equinox and evening audience to the moon outside the western gate at the autumn equinox were the proper and regular sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Only the spring-equinox morning audience to the sun outside the eastern gate and the autumn-equinox evening audience to the moon outside the western gate were proper, regular sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 蓋天地至尊，故用其始而祭以二至。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth are supreme; therefore their beginnings are honored and sacrifice is performed at the two solstices.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth are supreme; therefore their beginnings are honored with sacrifice at the two solstices.

sentences.zh: 日月次天地，春分陽氣方永，秋分陰氣向長，故祭以二分，爲得陰陽之義。

translations.literal: Sun and moon rank next to Heaven and Earth; at the spring equinox yang qi is just waxing, and at the autumn equinox yin qi is lengthening—therefore sacrifice at the two equinoxes accords with the meaning of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon stand next to Heaven and Earth; at the spring equinox yang force is rising and at the autumn equinox yin force is growing—sacrifice at the two equinoxes thus accords with yin-yang principle.

sentences.zh: 自秦祭八神，六曰月主，七曰日主，雍又有日月廟。

translations.literal: From Qin, eight spirits were sacrificed; the sixth was Lord of the Moon and the seventh Lord of the Sun; Yong also had sun and moon temples.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin onward eight spirits were sacrificed—the sixth Lord of the Moon and seventh Lord of the Sun—and Yong also had sun and moon temples.

sentences.zh: 漢郊太乙，朝日夕月改周法。

translations.literal: Han suburban sacrifice to Grand Unity changed Zhou institutions for morning sun and evening moon.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han suburban sacrifice to Grand Unity, morning sun and evening moon rites departed from Zhou practice.

sentences.zh: 常以郊泰畤，質明出行宮，東向揖日，西向揖月，又於殿下東西拜日月。

translations.literal: Regularly at suburban Tai altar, at dawn leaving the traveling palace, bow east to the sun and west to the moon; again east and west bow to sun and moon below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: At suburban Tai altar, at dawn leaving the traveling palace, they bowed east to the sun and west to the moon, and again bowed to sun and moon east and west below the hall.

sentences.zh: 宣帝於神山祠日，萊山祠月。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan sacrificed to the sun at the Spirit Mountain temple and to the moon at the Lai Mountain temple.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan sacrificed to the sun at Spirit Mountain and to the moon at Lai Mountain.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝始朝日東郊，夕月西郊。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei first performed morning sun in the eastern suburb and evening moon in the western suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei first instituted morning sun in the eastern suburb and evening moon in the western suburb.

sentences.zh: 唐以二分日，朝日夕月於國城東西。

translations.literal: Tang on the equinox days performed morning sun and evening moon east and west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tang performed morning sun and evening moon east and west of the capital on the equinox days.

sentences.zh: 宋人因之，升爲大祀。

translations.literal: Song followed this and elevated the rite to great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Song followed this practice and elevated the rites to great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 元郊壇以日月從祀，其二分朝日夕月，皇慶中議建立而未行。

translations.literal: Yuan suburban altar had sun and moon in attendant sacrifice; the equinox morning sun and evening moon were discussed for establishment under Huangqing but not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yuan suburban altar sun and moon were attendant sacrifices; equinox morning sun and evening moon were debated under Huangqing but never implemented.

sentences.zh: 今當稽古正祭之禮，各設壇專祀。

translations.literal: Now the orthodox sacrifice of antiquity should be examined, and separate altars established for dedicated sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The orthodox rites of antiquity should now be followed, with separate altars for dedicated sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 朝日壇宜築於城東門外，夕月壇宜築於城西門外。

translations.literal: The morning sun altar should be built outside the eastern city gate and the evening moon altar outside the western city gate.
translations.idiomatic: The morning sun altar should stand outside the eastern gate and the evening moon altar outside the western gate.

sentences.zh: 朝日以春分，夕月以秋分。

translations.literal: Morning sun at the spring equinox and evening moon at the autumn equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Morning sun at the spring equinox and evening moon at the autumn equinox.

sentences.zh: 星辰則祔祭於月壇。

translations.literal: The stars were attached in sacrifice at the moon altar.
translations.idiomatic: The stars were offered as attached sacrifice at the moon altar.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 其祀儀與社稷同。

translations.literal: The sacrificial protocol was the same as for state and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial protocol matched that for state and grain.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，帝以大明、夜明已從祀，罷朝日夕月之祭。

translations.literal: In year twenty-one the emperor, since Great Brightness and Night Brightness already received attendant sacrifice, abolished morning sun and evening moon sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, since Great Brightness and Night Brightness already received attendant sacrifice, the emperor abolished separate morning sun and evening moon offerings.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，帝謂「大報天而主日，配以月。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 9 the emperor said: "In great report to Heaven the sun is chief and the moon matched.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9 the emperor said: "In great report to Heaven the sun is chief and the moon matched.

sentences.zh: 大明壇當與夜明壇異。

translations.literal: The Great Brightness Altar should differ from the Night Brightness Altar.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Brightness altar should be distinct from the Night Brightness altar.

sentences.zh: 且日月照臨，其功甚大。

translations.literal: Moreover, sun and moon shine upon all; their merit is very great.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, sun and moon shine upon all beneath heaven—their merit is immense.

sentences.zh: 太歲等神，歲有二祭，而日月星辰止一從祭，義所不安」。

translations.literal: Spirits such as the Great Year receive two sacrifices a year, while sun, moon, and stars receive only one attendant sacrifice—the meaning is uneasy."
translations.idiomatic: Spirits such as the Great Year receive two sacrifices yearly, while sun, moon, and stars receive only one attendant sacrifice—the propriety is unsatisfying."

sentences.zh: 大學士張璁亦以爲缺典。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Cong also held this a missing ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Cong likewise held this a missing ritual.

sentences.zh: 遂定額春秋分之祭如舊儀，而建朝日壇於朝陽門外，西向；

translations.literal: Thereupon the fixed schedule of spring and autumn equinox sacrifice was restored as in old ritual, and the morning sun altar was built outside Chaoyang Gate, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: The fixed equinox schedule was restored, the morning sun altar built outside Chaoyang Gate facing west;

sentences.zh: 夕月壇於阜城門外，東向。

translations.literal: the evening moon altar outside Fucheng Gate, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: and the evening moon altar outside Fucheng Gate facing east.

sentences.zh: 壇制有隆殺以示別。

translations.literal: Altar regulations had gradation to show distinction.
translations.idiomatic: The altars were graded in scale to mark their distinction.

sentences.zh: 朝日，護壇地一百畝；

translations.literal: For morning sun, one hundred mu protected the altar ground;
translations.idiomatic: For morning sun, one hundred mu were set aside to protect the altar;

sentences.zh: 夕月，護壇地三十六畝。

translations.literal: for evening moon, thirty-six mu protected the altar ground.
translations.idiomatic: for evening moon, thirty-six mu.

sentences.zh: 朝日無從祀，夕月以五星、二十八宿、周天星辰共一罈，南向祔焉。

translations.literal: Morning sun had no attendant sacrifice; evening moon had the five planets, twenty-eight lodges, and all stars of the circuit on one altar, attached facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Morning sun had no attendants; at evening moon the five planets, twenty-eight lodges, and circuit stars shared one altar, attached facing south.

sentences.zh: 春祭，時以寅，迎日出也。

translations.literal: Spring sacrifice at the yin hour, welcoming the sun's rising.
translations.idiomatic: The spring rite was held at the yin hour, welcoming the rising sun.

sentences.zh: 秋祭，時以亥，迎月出也。

translations.literal: Autumn sacrifice at the hai hour, welcoming the moon's rising.
translations.idiomatic: The autumn rite at the hai hour, welcoming the rising moon.

sentences.zh: 十年，禮部上朝日、夕月儀：朝日迎神四拜，飲福受胙兩拜，送神四拜；

translations.literal: In year ten the Ministry of Rites submitted morning sun and evening moon protocol: morning sun—welcoming the spirit four bows, drinking the blessing and receiving the flesh two bows, sending off the spirit four bows;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Ministry of Rites submitted protocols: for morning sun, four bows welcoming the spirit, two bows drinking the blessing and receiving the flesh, four bows sending off the spirit;

sentences.zh: 夕月迎神飲福受胙送神皆再拜。

translations.literal: evening moon—welcoming the spirit, drinking the blessing, receiving the flesh, and sending off the spirit each two bows.
translations.idiomatic: for evening moon, two bows each for welcoming the spirit, drinking the blessing, receiving the flesh, and sending off the spirit.

sentences.zh: 餘並如舊儀。

translations.literal: The remainder followed old ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder followed former practice.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，禮部議定，東郊以甲、丙、戊、庚、壬年，西郊以醜、辰、未、戌年，車駕親祭。

translations.literal: In Longqing 1 the Ministry of Rites resolved that in the eastern suburb on jia, bing, wu, geng, and ren years and in the western suburb on chou, chen, wei, and xu years, the imperial carriage would sacrifice in person.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 1 the Ministry resolved that on jia, bing, wu, geng, and ren years the emperor would sacrifice in person at the eastern suburb, and on chou, chen, wei, and xu years at the western suburb.

sentences.zh: 餘歲遣文大臣攝祭朝日壇，武大臣攝祭夕月壇。

translations.literal: In other years a civil grand minister would deputize at the morning sun altar and a military grand minister at the evening moon altar.
translations.idiomatic: In other years a civil grand minister deputized at the morning sun altar and a military grand minister at the evening moon altar.

sentences.zh: 三年，禮部上朝日儀，言：「正祭遇風雨，則設小次於壇前，駕就小次行禮。

translations.literal: In year three the Ministry of Rites submitted morning sun protocol, saying: "If wind and rain occur at the orthodox sacrifice, a small shelter is set before the altar and the carriage performs rites at the shelter.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Ministry submitted morning sun protocol: "If rain falls during the orthodox sacrifice, a small shelter is erected before the altar and the emperor performs rites there.

sentences.zh: 其升降奠獻，俱以太常寺執事官代。

translations.literal: Ascent and descent, presentation and offering are all performed by Court of Imperial Sacrifices officiants in proxy.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent, descent, presentation, and offering are all performed by Court of Imperial Sacrifices officiants as proxies.

translations.literal: " The regulation read: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: " The regulation read: "Approved."

sentences.zh: ○先農

translations.literal: ● Former agriculture
translations.idiomatic: Former Agriculture

sentences.zh: 二年二月，帝建先農壇於南郊，在耤田北。

translations.literal: In the second month of year two the emperor built the Former Agriculture altar in the southern suburb, north of the plough field.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year, the emperor built the Former Agriculture altar in the southern suburb, north of the imperial plough field.

sentences.zh: 親祭，以後稷配。

translations.literal: He sacrificed in person, with Hou Ji as matched spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He sacrificed in person, with Hou Ji as paired spirit.

sentences.zh: 器物祀儀與社稷同。

translations.literal: Vessels, implements, and sacrificial protocol were the same as for state and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Vessels, implements, and protocol matched those for state and grain.

sentences.zh: 祀畢，行耕耤禮。

translations.literal: When sacrifice was complete, the plough-field rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: After sacrifice, the plough-field rite was performed.

sentences.zh: 御耒耜二具，韜以青絹，御耕牛四，被以青衣。

translations.literal: Two plough implements were used, wrapped in green silk; four plough oxen were draped in green cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Two imperial ploughs wrapped in green silk and four plough oxen draped in green cloth were prepared.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，還大次。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, he returned to the great shelter.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite ended, he returned to the great shelter.

sentences.zh: 應天府尹及上元、江寧兩縣令率庶人終畝。

translations.literal: The Shuntian prefect and the magistrates of Shangyuan and Jiangning led the commoners to finish the field.
translations.idiomatic: The Shuntian prefect and the magistrates of Shangyuan and Jiangning led commoners to finish ploughing the field.

sentences.zh: 是日，宴勞百官耆老於壇所，十年二月，遣官享先農，命應天府官率農民耆老陪祀。

translations.literal: That day, officials and elders were feasted and rewarded at the altar site; in the second month of year ten officials were dispatched to offer to Former Agriculture, ordering Shuntian officials to lead farmers and elders in attendant sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: That day officials and elders were feasted at the altar; in the tenth year, second month, officials were sent to sacrifice to Former Agriculture, with Shuntian officials leading farmers and elders in attendance.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，更定祭先農儀，不設配位。

translations.literal: In year twenty-one the Former Agriculture sacrifice was revised, with no matched spirit set.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the Former Agriculture rite was revised to omit paired spirits.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，建壇京師，如南京制，在太歲壇西南。

translations.literal: In the Yongle period an altar was built in the capital like the Nanjing model, southwest of the Great Year altar.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle an altar was built in the capital on the Nanjing model, southwest of the Great Year altar.

sentences.zh: 石階九級。

translations.literal: Stone steps of nine grades.
translations.idiomatic: It had nine stone steps.

sentences.zh: 西瘞位，東齋宮、鑾駕庫，東北神倉，東南具服殿，殿前爲觀耕之所。

translations.literal: Burial position to the west; fasting palace and imperial equipage storehouse to the east; spirit granary to the northeast; vestment hall to the southeast; before the hall was the place for viewing the ploughing.
translations.idiomatic: To the west was the burial position; to the east the fasting palace and equipage storehouse; northeast the spirit granary; southeast the vestment hall, before which lay the viewing ground for the ploughing.

sentences.zh: 護壇地六百畝，供黍稷及薦新品物地九十餘畝。

translations.literal: Six hundred mu protected the altar ground, with more than ninety mu supplying millet and new offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred mu protected the altar, with more than ninety mu for millet and new offerings.

sentences.zh: 每歲仲春上戊，順天府尹致祭。

translations.literal: Each year on the upper wu of mid-spring the Shuntian prefect performed sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Each year on the upper wu of mid-spring the Shuntian prefect offered sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 後凡遇登極之初，行耕耤禮，則親祭。

translations.literal: Later, whenever a new reign began and the plough-field rite was performed, the emperor sacrificed in person.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, at the start of each reign when the plough-field rite was held, the emperor sacrificed in person.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年，定耕耤儀：前期百官致齋。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi 1 the plough-field protocol was fixed: beforehand all officials fasted.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 1 the plough-field protocol was fixed: beforehand all officials fasted.

sentences.zh: 順天府官以耒耜及穜ＡＬ種進呈，內官仍捧出授之，由午門左出。

translations.literal: Shuntian officials presented plough implements and early and late grain seeds; inner palace attendants still bore them out and handed them over, exiting by the left of the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian officials presented ploughs and early and late grain seeds; inner attendants bore them out through the left of the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 置彩輿，鼓樂，送至耤田所。

translations.literal: They were placed in a decorated carriage with drums and music and sent to the plough field.
translations.idiomatic: They were placed in a decorated carriage with drums and music and sent to the plough field.

sentences.zh: 至期，帝翼善冠黃袍，詣壇所具服殿，服袞冕，祭先農。

translations.literal: On the day, the emperor in the Good Governance cap and yellow robe went to the vestment hall at the altar, donned the sacrificial robes, and sacrificed to Former Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the emperor, in the Good Governance cap and yellow robe, went to the vestment hall, donned sacrificial robes, and sacrificed to Former Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 畢，還，更翼善冠黃袍。

translations.literal: When complete, he returned and again wore the Good Governance cap and yellow robe.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, he returned and again wore the Good Governance cap and yellow robe.

sentences.zh: 太常卿導引至耕耤位，南向立。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices director guided him to the plough-field position, standing facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices director guided him to the ploughing station, facing south.

sentences.zh: 三公以下各就位，戶部尚書北向跪進耒耜，順天府官北向跪進鞭。

translations.literal: The Three Dukes and below each took position; the Minister of Revenue knelt facing north and presented the plough, and Shuntian officials knelt facing north and presented the whip.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dukes and others took their places; the Minister of Revenue knelt north and presented the plough, and Shuntian officials knelt north and presented the whip.

sentences.zh: 帝秉耒，三推三反訖，戶部尚書跪受耒耜，順天府官跪受鞭，太常卿奏請復位。

translations.literal: The emperor took the plough, pushed three furrows and returned three times; when finished the Minister of Revenue knelt to receive the plough and Shuntian officials knelt to receive the whip; the Court director reported request to return to position.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the plough, pushed three furrows and backed three times; the Minister of Revenue then knelt to receive the plough and Shuntian officials the whip, and the Court director reported his return to position.

sentences.zh: 府尹挾青箱以種子播而覆之。

translations.literal: The prefect carried a green box, broadcast seed and covered it.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect carried a green seed box, sowed seed, and covered it.

sentences.zh: 帝御外門，南向坐，觀三公五推，尚書九卿九推。

translations.literal: The emperor sat outside the gate facing south, watching the Three Dukes push five furrows and the nine ministers nine furrows.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sat outside the gate facing south, watching the Three Dukes plough five furrows and the nine ministers nine.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏耕畢，帝還具服殿，升座。

translations.literal: The Court director reported ploughing complete; the emperor returned to the vestment hall and ascended the seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Court director announced ploughing complete; the emperor returned to the vestment hall and took his seat.

sentences.zh: 府尹率兩縣令耆老人行禮畢，引上中下農夫各十人，執農器朝見，令其終畝。

translations.literal: The prefect led the two county magistrates and elders in completing the rites, then brought forward upper, middle, and lower farmers, ten of each, bearing farm tools to audience, and ordered them to finish the field.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect led the two county magistrates and elders through the closing rites, then presented ten upper, middle, and lower farmers each, bearing tools in audience, and ordered them to finish the field.

sentences.zh: 百官行慶賀禮，賜酒饌。

translations.literal: Officials performed congratulatory rites and wine and food were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials performed congratulatory rites and bestowed wine and food.

sentences.zh: 三品以上丹陛上東西坐，四品以下臺下坐，並宴勞耆老於壇旁。

translations.literal: Third rank and above sat east and west on the red steps; fourth rank and below sat below the terrace; elders were also feasted and rewarded beside the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above sat east and west on the red steps; fourth rank and below on the terrace below; elders were feasted beside the altar.

sentences.zh: 宴畢，駕還宮。

translations.literal: When the feast was complete, the carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the feast ended, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 大樂鼓吹振作，農夫人賜布一匹。

translations.literal: Great music and drums sounded; each farming household was given one bolt of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Great music sounded; each farming household received one bolt of cloth.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年，帝以其禮過煩，命禮官更定。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 10 the emperor held its ritual overly elaborate and ordered ritual officials to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 10 the emperor found the rite overly elaborate and ordered ritual officials to revise it.

sentences.zh: 迎神送神止行二拜。

translations.literal: Welcoming and sending off the spirit were reduced to two bows only.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming and sending off the spirit were reduced to two bows each.

sentences.zh: 先二日，順天府尹以耒耜穜ＡＬ種置彩輿，至耕耤所，並罷百官慶賀。

translations.literal: Two days beforehand the Shuntian prefect placed ploughs and early and late grain seeds in a decorated carriage and sent them to the plough field, and officials' congratulatory rites were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before, the Shuntian prefect sent ploughs and early and late grain seeds in a decorated carriage to the plough field, and officials' congratulatory rites were abolished.

sentences.zh: 後又議造耕根車載耒耜，府尹於祭日進呈畢，以耒耜載車內前玉輅行。

translations.literal: Later it was proposed to build a Plough-Root carriage to carry the plough; the prefect on the sacrifice day would present them and load the plough into the carriage to proceed before the jade chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Later a Plough-Root carriage was proposed to carry the plough; on the sacrifice day the prefect would present them and load the plough into the carriage to proceed before the jade chariot.

sentences.zh: 其御門觀耕，地位卑下，議建觀耕臺一。

translations.literal: Viewing the ploughing from the imperial gate—the position was too low; it was proposed to build one Viewing-the-Ploughing terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Viewing the ploughing from the imperial gate left the vantage too low; a Viewing-the-Ploughing terrace was proposed.

sentences.zh: 詔皆可。

translations.literal: An edict approved all.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved all proposals.

sentences.zh: 後又命墾西苑隙地爲田。

translations.literal: Later an order was also given to reclaim vacant land in the Western Park as fields.
translations.idiomatic: He later ordered vacant land in the Western Park reclaimed as fields.

sentences.zh: 建殿曰無逸，亭曰豳風，又曰省耕，曰省斂，倉曰恆裕。

translations.literal: A hall was built called No Dissipation, a pavilion called Binfeng, another called Inspecting the Plough, another Inspecting the Harvest, and a granary called Ever Abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Halls and pavilions were built: No Dissipation, Binfeng, Inspecting the Plough, Inspecting the Harvest, and a granary called Ever Abundant.

sentences.zh: 禮部上郊廟粢盛支給之數，因言：「南郊耤田，皇上三推，公卿各宣其力，較西苑爲重。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites submitted the numbers for suburban and temple grain offerings, saying: "For the southern suburb plough field, the emperor performs three furrows and the dukes and ministers each exert their strength—this weighs more than the Western Park.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites reported grain allotments for suburban and temple offerings, arguing: "At the southern-suburb plough field the emperor ploughs three furrows and the dukes and ministers each do their part—weighing more than the Western Park.

sentences.zh: 西苑雖農官督理，皇上時省耕斂，較耤田爲勤。

translations.literal: Although the Western Park is supervised by agricultural officials, the emperor from time to time inspects ploughing and harvest—more diligent than the plough field.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Western Park is overseen by agricultural officials, the emperor personally inspects ploughing and harvest there—more attentive than at the plough field.

sentences.zh: 請以耤田所出，藏南郊圓廩神倉，以供圜丘、祈谷、先農、神祇壇、長陵等陵、歷代帝王及百神之祀。

translations.literal: It is requested that produce from the plough field be stored in the southern suburb round granary and spirit granary, to supply sacrifice at the Circular Mound, Prayer for Grain, Former Agriculture, Spirit Altars, Changling and other tombs, successive emperors, and the hundred spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Produce from the plough field should be stored in the southern suburb round and spirit granaries for the Circular Mound, Prayer for Grain, Former Agriculture, spirit altars, imperial tombs, successive emperors, and the hundred spirits.

sentences.zh: 西苑所出，藏恆裕倉，以供方澤、朝日、夕月、太廟、世廟、太社稷、帝社稷、禘佩、先蠶及先師孔子之祀。

translations.literal: Produce from the Western Park should be stored in the Ever Abundant granary, to supply sacrifice at the Square Mound, morning sun, evening moon, Grand Ancestral Temple, Imperial Ancestral Temple, Grand State and Grain, Imperial State and Grain, dipei, Former Silkworms, and Former Teacher Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Western Park produce should go to the Ever Abundant granary for the Square Mound, morning sun, evening moon, Grand and Imperial Ancestral Temples, state and grain altars, dipei, Former Silkworms, and Confucius.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 十六年，諭凡遇親耕，則戶部尚書先祭先農。

translations.literal: In year sixteen an instruction was given that whenever personal ploughing occurred, the Minister of Revenue should first sacrifice to Former Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year it was ordered that before personal ploughing, the Minister of Revenue should sacrifice to Former Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 皇帝至，止行三推禮。

translations.literal: When the emperor arrived, only the three-furrow rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's arrival, only the three-furrow rite was performed.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，罷親耕，惟遣官祭先農。

translations.literal: In year thirty-eight personal ploughing was abolished; only officials were dispatched to sacrifice to Former Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year personal ploughing ended; only dispatched officials sacrificed to Former Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，並令所司勿復奏。

translations.literal: In year forty-one the responsible offices were also ordered not to memorialize again.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year responsible offices were told to cease memorializing on the matter.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，罷西苑耕種諸祀，皆取之耤田。

translations.literal: In Longqing 1 Western Park ploughing and related sacrifices were abolished; all were taken from the plough field.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 1 Western Park cultivation and its related sacrifices were abolished; all grain came from the plough field.

sentences.zh: ○先蠶

translations.literal: ● Former silkworms
translations.idiomatic: Former Silkworms

sentences.zh: 明初未列祀典。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming they were not listed in the sacrificial canon.
translations.idiomatic: In early Ming they were not listed in the sacrificial canon.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖時，都給事中夏言請改各宮莊田爲親蠶廠公桑園。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing period Supervising Secretary Xia Yan of the Secretariat requested converting various palace estate fields into personal silkworm factories and public mulberry gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing, Supervising Secretary Xia Yan asked to convert palace estate fields into imperial silkworm grounds and public mulberry gardens.

sentences.zh: 令有司種桑柘，以備宮中蠶事。

translations.literal: Officials were ordered to plant mulberry and catalpa to supply palace silkworm work.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were ordered to plant mulberry and catalpa for palace sericulture.

sentences.zh: 九年，復疏言，耕蠶之禮，不宜偏廢。

translations.literal: In year nine he again memorialized that ploughing and silkworm rites should not be neglected on one side.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he again argued that ploughing and silkworm rites should not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 帝乃敕禮部：「古者天子親耕，皇后親蠶，以勸天下。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered the Ministry of Rites: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven ploughed in person and the queen raised silkworms in person, to encourage all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven ploughed and the queen raised silkworms in person, to encourage the realm.

sentences.zh: 自今歲始，朕親祀先農，皇后親蠶，其考古制，具儀以聞。

translations.literal: From this year I shall sacrifice in person to Former Agriculture and the queen shall raise silkworms in person; examine ancient institutions and report the full protocol.
translations.idiomatic: "From this year I shall sacrifice to Former Agriculture in person and the queen raise silkworms in person; examine antiquity and submit the full protocol."

sentences.zh: 」大學士張璁等請於安定門外建先蠶壇。

translations.literal: " Grand Secretary Zhang Cong and others requested building a Former Silkworms altar outside Anding Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Cong and others proposed a Former Silkworms altar outside Anding Gate.

sentences.zh: 詹事霍韜以道遠爭之。

translations.literal: Director of the Heir Apparent Huo Tao objected on grounds of distance.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Heir Apparent Huo Tao objected that it was too far.

sentences.zh: 戶部亦言：「安定門外近西之地，水源不通，無浴蠶所。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue also said: "Land near the west outside Anding Gate has no flowing water and no place for bathing silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue added: "Land west of Anding Gate lacks running water and a place to bathe silkworms.

sentences.zh: 皇城內西苑中有太液、瓊島之水。

translations.literal: Within the imperial city the Western Park has the waters of Supreme Fluidity and Jade Isle.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Park within the imperial city has the waters of Supreme Fluidity and Jade Isle.

sentences.zh: 考唐制在苑中，宋亦在宮中，宜仿行之。

translations.literal: Examining Tang institutions, they were in the park; Song also placed them within the palace—this should be imitated.
translations.idiomatic: Tang placed the rite in the park; Song within the palace—these models should be followed.

sentences.zh: 」帝謂唐人因陋就安，不可法。

translations.literal: " The emperor said Tang people made do with what was at hand and should not be taken as law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that Tang practice was makeshift and should not be followed.

sentences.zh: 於是禮部尚書李時等言：「大明門至安定門，道路遙遠，請鳳輦出東華、玄武二門。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minister of Rites Li Shi and others said: "From Daming Gate to Anding Gate the road is long; the phoenix carriage should exit by the Donghua and Xuanwu gates.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Li Shi and others argued: "The route from Daming Gate to Anding Gate was too long; the imperial carriage should exit by the Donghua and Xuanwu gates.

sentences.zh: 」因條上四事：一、治繭之禮，二、壇壝之向，三、採桑之器，四、掌壇之官。

translations.literal: " They then listed four items: first, the cocoon-treating rite; second, the orientation of altar and mound; third, mulberry-picking implements; fourth, officials in charge of the altar.
translations.idiomatic: They listed four points: cocoon-treating ritual, altar orientation, mulberry-picking implements, and altar officials.

sentences.zh: 帝從其言，命自玄武門出。

translations.literal: The emperor followed their words and ordered exit by the Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered exit by the Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 內使陳儀衛，軍一萬人，五千圍壇所，五千護於道，餘如議。

translations.literal: Inner attendants arranged guards; ten thousand troops—five thousand surrounding the altar, five thousand guarding the route—the rest as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants arranged guards: ten thousand troops, half encircling the altar and half along the route, with the rest as proposed.

sentences.zh: 二月，工部上先蠶壇圖式，帝親定其制。

translations.literal: In the second month the Ministry of Works submitted the Former Silkworms altar plan; the emperor personally fixed its form.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Ministry of Works submitted altar plans, which the emperor personally approved.

sentences.zh: 壇方二丈六尺，疊二級，高二尺六寸，四出陛。

translations.literal: The altar was twenty-six chi square, two tiers, two chi six cun high, with steps on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The altar was twenty-six chi square, two tiers high at two chi six cun, with steps on four sides.

sentences.zh: 東西北俱樹桑柘，內設蠶宮令署。

translations.literal: East, north, and west were planted with mulberry and catalpa; within was set the Silkworm Office.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberry and catalpa were planted to the east, north, and west; within stood the Silkworm Office.

sentences.zh: 採桑臺高一尺四寸，方十倍，三出陛。

translations.literal: The mulberry-picking terrace was one chi four cun high, ten times the altar's width, with steps on three sides.
translations.idiomatic: The mulberry-picking terrace was one chi four cun high, ten times the altar's width, with steps on three sides.

sentences.zh: 鑾駕庫五間。

translations.literal: Five bays of imperial equipage storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Five bays of imperial equipage storehouse were built.

sentences.zh: 後蓋織堂。

translations.literal: Behind was the Reeling Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Behind stood the Reeling Hall.

sentences.zh: 壇圍方八十丈。

translations.literal: The altar enclosure was eighty zhang square.
translations.idiomatic: The altar enclosure measured eighty zhang square.

sentences.zh: 禮部上皇后親蠶儀：蠶將生，欽天監擇吉巳日以聞。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites submitted the queen's personal silkworm protocol: when silkworms were about to hatch, the Directorate of Astronomy chose an auspicious si day and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry submitted the queen's silkworm protocol: when eggs were about to hatch, the Directorate of Astronomy chose an auspicious si day and reported it.

sentences.zh: 順天府具蠶母名數送北郊，工部以鉤箔筐架諸器物給蠶母。

translations.literal: Shuntian prefecture supplied the names and numbers of silkworm mothers to the northern suburb; the Ministry of Works provided hooks, trays, frames, and other implements to the silkworm mothers.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian supplied silkworm mothers to the northern suburb; the Ministry of Works provided hooks, trays, frames, and other tools.

sentences.zh: 順天府以蠶種及鉤筐一進呈，內官捧出，還授之。

translations.literal: Shuntian presented silkworm eggs and one hook-tray set; inner attendants bore them out and returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian presented silkworm eggs and a hook-tray set; inner attendants bore them out and back.

sentences.zh: 出玄武右門，置彩輿中，鼓樂送至蠶室。

translations.literal: Exiting by the right of Xuanwu Gate, they were placed in a decorated carriage with drums and music and sent to the silkworm chamber.
translations.idiomatic: They exited right of Xuanwu Gate, were placed in a decorated carriage with drums and music, and sent to the silkworm chamber.

sentences.zh: 蠶母受蠶種，浴飼以待。

translations.literal: The silkworm mothers received the eggs, bathed and fed them, and waited.
translations.idiomatic: Silkworm mothers received the eggs, bathed and fed them, and waited.

sentences.zh: 命婦文四品、武三品以上俱陪祀，攜一侍女執鉤筐。

translations.literal: Ordered wives of civil officials of the fourth rank and above and military officials of the third rank and above all attended sacrifice, each bringing one attendant maid bearing a hook-tray.
translations.idiomatic: Wives of civil officials fourth rank and above and military officials third rank and above attended, each with a maid bearing a hook-tray.

sentences.zh: 皇后齋三日，內執事並司贊、六尚等女官及應入壇者齋一日。

translations.literal: The queen fasted three days; inner attendants, ritual directors, the Six Bureaus, and all women entering the altar fasted one day.
translations.idiomatic: The queen fasted three days; inner attendants, ritual directors, the Six Bureaus, and all women entering the altar fasted one day.

sentences.zh: 先一日，太常寺具祝版，祭物，羊、豕、籩豆各六、黑帛，送蠶宮令。

translations.literal: One day beforehand the Court of Imperial Sacrifices prepared prayer tablets and offerings—sheep, swine, six platters each of baskets and beans, and black silk—and sent them to the Silkworm Office director.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices prepared prayer tablets and offerings—sheep, swine, platters, beans, and black silk—and sent them to the Silkworm Office.

sentences.zh: 是日，分授執事女官。

translations.literal: That day they were distributed to officiating women.
translations.idiomatic: That day offerings were distributed to officiating women.

sentences.zh: 日未明。

translations.literal: Before the sun had risen.
translations.idiomatic: Before sunrise.

sentences.zh: 宿衛陳兵備，女樂司設監備儀仗及重翟車，俱候玄武門外。

translations.literal: Guards arrayed arms; the female musicians bureau prepared regalia and the heavy pheasant carriage, all waiting outside Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Guards arrayed arms; the female musicians prepared regalia and the heavy pheasant carriage outside Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 將明，內侍詣坤寧宮奏請。

translations.literal: As dawn approached, inner attendants went to the Kunning Palace to report.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn inner attendants reported at Kunning Palace.

sentences.zh: 皇后服常服，導引女官導出宮門，乘肩輿，至玄武門。

translations.literal: The queen in ordinary dress, guided by women, left the palace gate, rode a shoulder carriage to Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The queen in ordinary dress, guided out, rode a shoulder carriage to Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 內侍奏請降輿，升重翟車。

translations.literal: Inner attendants reported request to descend and mount the heavy pheasant carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants asked her to descend and mount the heavy pheasant carriage.

sentences.zh: 兵衛儀仗及女樂前導，出北安門，障以行帷，至壇內壝東門。

translations.literal: Arms guards and female musicians led before; exiting North An Gate, screened by traveling curtains to the inner east gate of the altar enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Guards and musicians led; exiting North An Gate behind curtains to the altar's inner east gate.

sentences.zh: 內侍奏請降車，乘肩輿，兵衛、儀仗停東門外。

translations.literal: Inner attendants reported request to descend; she rode a shoulder carriage; arms guards and regalia halted outside the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: She descended to a shoulder carriage; guards and regalia halted outside the east gate.

sentences.zh: 皇后入具服殿，易禮服，出，至壇。

translations.literal: The queen entered the vestment hall, changed to ritual dress, and came out to the altar.
translations.idiomatic: She entered the vestment hall, donned ritual dress, and proceeded to the altar.

sentences.zh: 司贊奏就位。

translations.literal: The ritual director reported taking position.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual director announced taking position.

sentences.zh: 公主、內外命婦各就拜位。

translations.literal: Princesses and inner and outer ordered wives each took bowing positions.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses and inner and outer ordered wives took their bowing positions.

sentences.zh: 祭先蠶，行三獻禮，女官執事如儀。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to Former Silkworms was performed with the three-offering rite; women officiants acted as protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Former Silkworms sacrifice followed the three-offering rite, with women officiants.

sentences.zh: 迎神四拜，賜福胙二拜，送神四拜。

translations.literal: Welcoming the spirit four bows, receiving blessing and flesh two bows, sending off the spirit four bows.
translations.idiomatic: Four bows welcoming the spirit, two bows receiving blessing and flesh, four bows sending off the spirit.

sentences.zh: 凡拜跪興，公主、內外命婦皆同。

translations.literal: In all bowing, kneeling, and rising, princesses and inner and outer ordered wives were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses and ordered wives bowed, knelt, and rose in unison.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，皇后還具服殿，更常服。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete the queen returned to the vestment hall and changed to ordinary dress.
translations.idiomatic: When finished she returned to the vestment hall and changed to ordinary dress.

sentences.zh: 司賓引外命婦先詣採桑壇東陛下，南北向。

translations.literal: The guest director led outer ordered wives first to the east steps of the mulberry-picking terrace, facing south and north.
translations.idiomatic: The guest director led outer ordered wives to the mulberry terrace's east steps, facing north and south.

sentences.zh: 尚儀奏請，皇后詣採桑位，東向。

translations.literal: The chief of ceremonies reported request; the queen went to the mulberry position, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The chief of ceremonies announced; the queen went to the mulberry position, facing east.

sentences.zh: 公主以下位皇后位東，亦南北向，以西爲上。

translations.literal: Princesses and below stood east of the queen, also facing south and north, with west as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses and others stood east of the queen, also north-south oriented, with west as senior.

sentences.zh: 執鉤者跪進鉤，執筐者跪奉筐受桑。

translations.literal: Hook-bearers knelt and presented hooks; tray-bearers knelt and presented trays to receive mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: Hook-bearers knelt with hooks; tray-bearers knelt with trays to receive mulberry.

sentences.zh: 皇后採桑三條，還至壇南儀門坐，觀命婦採桑。

translations.literal: The queen picked three mulberry sprays, returned to sit at the south ceremonial gate of the altar, and watched ordered wives pick mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: The queen picked three sprays, then sat at the altar's south gate watching ordered wives pick mulberry.

sentences.zh: 三公命婦採五條，列侯、九卿命婦採九條。

translations.literal: Wives of the Three Dukes picked five sprays; wives of marquises and nine ministers picked nine sprays.
translations.idiomatic: Wives of the Three Dukes picked five sprays; wives of marquises and nine ministers nine.

sentences.zh: 訖，各授女侍。

translations.literal: When finished, each handed them to female attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When done, each gave them to female attendants.

sentences.zh: 司賓引內命婦一人，詣桑室，尚功率執鉤筐者從。

translations.literal: The guest director led one inner ordered wife to the silkworm chamber, with the chief of accomplishments and hook-tray bearers following.
translations.idiomatic: The guest director led one inner ordered wife to the silkworm chamber, with the chief of accomplishments and tray-bearers following.
