sentences.zh: 尚功以桑授蠶母。

translations.literal: The chief of accomplishments gave mulberry to the silkworm mothers.
translations.idiomatic: The chief of accomplishments gave mulberry to the silkworm mothers.

sentences.zh: 蠶母受桑，縷切之，以授內命婦。

translations.literal: The silkworm mothers received mulberry, stripped and cut it, and gave it to inner ordered wives.
translations.idiomatic: Silkworm mothers received mulberry, stripped and cut it, and gave it to inner ordered wives.

sentences.zh: 內命婦食蠶，灑一箔訖，還。

translations.literal: Inner ordered wives fed the silkworms, sprinkled one tray, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Inner ordered wives fed the silkworms, sprinkled one tray, and returned.

sentences.zh: 尚儀奏禮畢，皇后還坐具服殿。

translations.literal: The chief of ceremonies reported the rite complete; the queen returned to sit in the vestment hall.
translations.idiomatic: The chief of ceremonies announced completion; the queen returned to the vestment hall.

sentences.zh: 司賓率蠶母等叩頭訖，司贊唱班齊。

translations.literal: The guest director led silkworm mothers and others to kowtow; the ritual director called the ranks to align.
translations.idiomatic: The guest director led silkworm mothers to kowtow; the ritual director aligned the ranks.

sentences.zh: 外名婦序立定，尚儀致詞云：「親蠶既成，禮當慶賀。

translations.literal: Outer ordered wives stood in order; the chief of ceremonies spoke: "Personal silkworm work is complete; congratulations are due.
translations.idiomatic: Outer ordered wives stood in order; the chief of ceremonies said: "Personal silkworm work is complete; congratulations are due.

sentences.zh: 」四拜畢，賜宴命婦，並賜蠶母酒食。

translations.literal: " Four bows complete; a feast was given to ordered wives, and wine and food to silkworm mothers.
translations.idiomatic: " After four bows, ordered wives were feasted and silkworm mothers given wine and food.

sentences.zh: 公主及內命婦於殿內，外命婦文武二品以上於臺上，三品以下於丹墀，尚食進膳。

translations.literal: Princesses and inner ordered wives inside the hall; outer ordered wives of civil and military second rank and above on the terrace; third rank and below on the red steps; the chief of food served the meal.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses and inner ordered wives dined inside; outer ordered wives second rank and above on the terrace; third rank and below on the red steps; the chief of food served.

sentences.zh: 教坊司女樂奏樂。

translations.literal: Female musicians of the Music Office performed.
translations.idiomatic: Female musicians of the Music Office performed.

sentences.zh: 宴畢，公主以下各就班四拜。

translations.literal: When the feast was complete, princesses and below each took position and bowed four times.
translations.idiomatic: When the feast ended, princesses and others bowed four times from position.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，皇后還宮，導從前。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete the queen returned to the palace, with escort before.
translations.idiomatic: The queen returned to the palace with escort before.

sentences.zh: 詔如擬。

translations.literal: An edict approved as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved as proposed.

sentences.zh: 四月，蠶事告成，行治繭禮。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, when silkworm work was reported complete, the cocoon-treating rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, when sericulture was complete, the cocoon-treating rite was held.

sentences.zh: 選蠶婦善繅絲及織者各十人。

translations.literal: Ten skilled women at reeling silk and ten at weaving were selected.
translations.idiomatic: Ten skilled reelers and ten weavers were selected.

sentences.zh: 卜日，皇后出宮，導從如常儀，至織堂。

translations.literal: An auspicious day was chosen; the queen left the palace with escort as usual to the Reeling Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On an auspicious day the queen left the palace with usual escort to the Reeling Hall.

sentences.zh: 內命婦一人行三盆手禮，佈於織婦，以終其事。

translations.literal: One inner ordered wife performed the three-basin hand rite and distributed work to weaving women to complete the task.
translations.idiomatic: One inner ordered wife performed the three-basin hand rite and assigned work to weavers to finish.

sentences.zh: 蠶宮令送尚衣織染監局造祭服，其祀先蠶，止用樂，不用舞，樂女生冠服俱用黑。

translations.literal: The Silkworm Office director sent silk to the Imperial Apparel Weaving and Dyeing Directorate to make sacrificial robes; sacrifice to Former Silkworms used music only, no dance; female musicians' caps and robes were all black.
translations.idiomatic: The Silkworm Office sent silk to the Weaving Directorate for sacrificial robes; Former Silkworms sacrifice used music without dance; female musicians wore black.

sentences.zh: 十年二月，禮臣言：「去歲皇后躬行採桑，已足風勵天下。

translations.literal: In the second month of year ten ritual officials said: "Last year the queen personally picked mulberry, sufficient to encourage all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, second month, ritual officials said: "Last year the queen picked mulberry in person, enough to encourage the realm.

sentences.zh: 今先蠶壇殿工未畢，宜且遣官行禮。

translations.literal: Now the Former Silkworms altar halls are not yet finished; officials should perform the rite for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: The altar halls are unfinished; officials should perform the rite for now.

sentences.zh: 」帝初不可，令如舊行。

translations.literal: " The emperor at first refused, ordering performance as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first refused, ordering the former practice.

sentences.zh: 已而以皇后出入不便，命改築先蠶壇於西苑。

translations.literal: Later, because the queen's coming and going was inconvenient, an order was given to rebuild the Former Silkworms altar in the Western Park.
translations.idiomatic: Later, finding the queen's travel inconvenient, he ordered the altar rebuilt in the Western Park.

sentences.zh: 壇之東爲採桑臺，臺東爲具服殿，北爲蠶室，左右爲廂房，其後爲從室，以居蠶婦。

translations.literal: East of the altar was the mulberry-picking terrace; east of the terrace the vestment hall; north the silkworm chamber; left and right wing rooms; behind, subsidiary rooms for silkworm women.
translations.idiomatic: East of the altar stood the mulberry terrace, east of that the vestment hall, north the silkworm chamber, with wing rooms and rear quarters for silkworm women.

sentences.zh: 設蠶宮署於宮左，令一員，丞二員，擇內臣謹恪者爲之。

translations.literal: A Silkworm Office was set to the left of the palace, with one director, two assistants, chosen from prudent inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: A Silkworm Office was established palace-left, with one director and two assistants chosen from prudent eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 四月，皇后行親蠶禮於內苑。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the queen performed personal silkworm rites in the inner park.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the queen performed personal silkworm rites in the inner park.

sentences.zh: 帝謂親耕無賀，此安得賀，第行叩頭禮，女樂第供宴，勿前導。

translations.literal: The emperor said personal ploughing had no congratulation—how could this have congratulation; only the kowtow rite was performed; female musicians supplied only the feast, not leading before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said personal ploughing had no congratulatory rite—this should have only kowtow; female musicians supplied the feast but did not lead the procession.

sentences.zh: 三十八年罷，親蠶禮。

translations.literal: In year thirty-eight the personal silkworm rite was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year the personal silkworm rite was abolished.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，並罷所司奏請。

translations.literal: In year forty-one memorial requests from responsible offices were also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year responsible offices were told to cease memorializing.

sentences.zh: ○高禖

translations.literal: ● High altars of procreation
translations.idiomatic: High Altars of Procreation

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，青州儒生李時颺請祠高禖，以祈聖嗣。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 9 the Qingzhou scholar Li Shiyang requested sacrifice to the High Altars of Procreation to pray for an imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9 Qingzhou scholar Li Shiyang requested sacrifice to the High Altars of Procreation to pray for an heir.

sentences.zh: 禮官覆以聞。

translations.literal: Ritual officials replied in memorial to report.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials memorialized in reply.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「高禖雖古禮，今實難行。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The High Altars of Procreation are ancient ritual, but in truth difficult to perform today.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The High Altars of Procreation are ancient ritual, but truly difficult to perform today.

sentences.zh: 」遂寢其議。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 已而定祀高禖禮。

translations.literal: Thereafter the ritual for sacrificing to the High Altars of Procreation was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The rite for sacrifice at the High Altars of Procreation was then established.

sentences.zh: 設木臺於皇城東，永安門北，震方。

translations.literal: A wooden platform was set up east of the Imperial City, north of Yong'an Gate, in the direction of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: A wooden platform was erected east of the Imperial City, north of Yong'an Gate, in the east—the Zhen direction.

sentences.zh: 臺上，皇天上帝南向，騂犢，蒼壁。

translations.literal: On the platform, the Supreme Lord of Imperial Heaven faced south, with a red bullock and a green jade disk.
translations.idiomatic: Upon the platform the Supreme Lord of Imperial Heaven faced south, offered a red bullock and a blue-green jade bi.

sentences.zh: 獻皇帝配，西向，牛羊豕各一。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was matched as associate, facing west, with one ox, one sheep, and one pig each.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor was paired as associate deity, facing west, with one ox, one sheep, and one pig.

sentences.zh: 高禖在壇下西向，牲數如之，禮三獻。

translations.literal: The High Altars of Procreation were below the altar facing west; the number of sacrificial animals was the same; the rite used three offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The High Altars of Procreation stood below the altar facing west, with the same offering counts, performed as a three-oblation rite.

sentences.zh: 皇帝位壇下北向，后妃位南數十丈外，北向，用帷。

translations.literal: The emperor stood below the altar facing north; the empress and consorts stood several tens of paces to the south, facing north, screened by curtains.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his place below the altar facing north; the empress and imperial consorts stood dozens of paces farther south, facing north behind curtains.

sentences.zh: 壇下陳弓矢、弓韣如后妃嬪之數。

translations.literal: Below the altar were displayed bows and arrows and bow cases in number matching the empress, consorts, and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Bows, arrows, and bow cases were laid out below the altar, one set for each empress, consort, and concubine.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，女官導后妃嬪至高禖前，跪取弓矢授后妃嬪，后妃嬪受而納於弓韣。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was finished, female officials led the empress, consorts, and concubines before the High Altars of Procreation; kneeling, they took up the bows and arrows and handed them to the empress, consorts, and concubines, who received them and placed them in the bow cases.
translations.idiomatic: After the sacrifice, female officials escorted the empress and consorts to the High Altars of Procreation, knelt, took up the bows and arrows, and handed them over; each woman received hers and put it into its bow case.

sentences.zh: ○祭告

translations.literal: ● Sacrificial announcements
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial Announcements

sentences.zh: 明制，凡登極、巡幸及上諡、葬陵、冊立、冊封、冠婚等事，皆祭告天地、宗廟、社稷。

translations.literal: Under Ming institutions, for all such matters as accession to the throne, imperial tours, bestowal of posthumous titles, burial of imperial tombs, investiture of the heir, enfeoffment, capping, and marriage, sacrificial announcements were made to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the state and grain altars.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming regulations, accession, imperial tours, posthumous honors, imperial burials, investiture of heirs, enfeoffments, capping ceremonies, and royal marriages all required sacrificial announcements to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the state and grain altars.

sentences.zh: 凡營造宮室，及命將出師，歲時旱潦，祭告天地、山川、太廟、社稷、后土。

translations.literal: For constructing palaces, commissioning generals for campaigns, and seasonal drought or flood, announcements were made to Heaven and Earth, mountains and rivers, the Grand Ancestral Temple, state and grain altars, and Empress Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Palace construction, dispatching armies, and seasonal drought or flood likewise called for announcements to Heaven and Earth, mountains and rivers, the Grand Ancestral Temple, the state and grain altars, and Empress Earth.

sentences.zh: 凡即位之初，並祭告闕里孔廟及歷代帝王陵寢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of every reign, announcements were also made at the Confucian temple in Queli and the tombs of emperors of successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of each reign, announcements were also made at the Confucius temple in Queli and at the tombs of emperors of past dynasties.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，禮部尚書崔亮奏，圜丘、方丘、大祀，前期親告太廟，仍遣使告百神於天下神祇壇。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 2 Minister of Rites Cui Liang memorialized: for the Circular Mound, Square Mound, and great sacrifice, in the preliminary period the emperor personally announced to the Grand Ancestral Temple, while still dispatching envoys to announce to the hundred spirits at the Altar of Spirits Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2 Minister of Rites Cui Liang reported that before the Circular Mound, Square Mound, and great sacrifices, the emperor would personally announce at the Grand Ancestral Temple and still send envoys to announce to the hundred spirits at the Altar of Spirits Under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 六年，禮部尚書牛諒奏，太歲諸神，凡祈報，則設一十五壇，有事祭告，則設神位二十八壇。

translations.literal: In year 6 Minister of Rites Niu Liang memorialized: for the Great Year and other spirits, for prayer and report altogether fifteen altars were set up; when there were matters to announce, twenty-eight altars with spirit seats were set up.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 6 Minister of Rites Niu Liang reported that for prayer and seasonal report rites to the Great Year and associated spirits, fifteen altars were erected; when special announcements were needed, twenty-eight altars with spirit seats were set up.

sentences.zh: 中，太歲、風雲雷雨、五嶽、五鎮、四海，凡五壇。

translations.literal: In the center: Great Year, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, the Five Peaks, the Five Garrisons, and the Four Seas—in all five altars.
translations.idiomatic: In the center stood five altars: Great Year; wind, clouds, thunder, and rain; the Five Peaks; the Five Garrisons; and the Four Seas.

sentences.zh: 東，四瀆、京畿、湖廣、山東、河南、北平、廣西、四川、甘肅山川，夏冬二季月將，京都城隍，凡十二壇。

translations.literal: To the east: the Four Rivers, the capital region, Huguang, Shandong, Henan, Beiping, Guangxi, Sichuan, Gansu mountains and rivers, the summer and winter seasonal monthly generals, and the capital city god—in all twelve altars.
translations.idiomatic: To the east were twelve altars: the Four Rivers; mountains and rivers of the capital region, Huguang, Shandong, Henan, Beiping, Guangxi, Sichuan, and Gansu; the summer and winter monthly generals; and the capital city god.

sentences.zh: 西，鐘山，江西、浙江、福建、山西、廣東、遼東山川，春秋二季月將，旗纛、戰船等神，凡十一罈。

translations.literal: To the west: Zhong Mountain; mountains and rivers of Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Shanxi, Guangdong, and Liaodong; the spring and autumn seasonal monthly generals; and spirits of banners, standards, and warships—in all eleven altars.
translations.idiomatic: To the west were eleven altars: Zhong Mountain; regional mountains and rivers from Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Shanxi, Guangdong, and Liaodong; the spring and autumn monthly generals; and spirits of banners, standards, and warships.

sentences.zh: 若親祀，皇帝皮弁服行一獻禮，每三壇行一次禮。

translations.literal: If the emperor sacrificed in person, he wore the skin cap and performed one offering at each rite; for every three altars he performed one round of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrificing in person, the emperor wore the skin cap and performed a single oblation, conducting one round of rites for every three altars.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝駐蹕中都，祭告天地於中都之圜丘。

translations.literal: In year 8 the emperor halted at Zhongdu and announced Heaven and Earth at Zhongdu's Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 8 the emperor sojourned at Zhongdu and announced Heaven and Earth at its Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 九年，以諸王將之籓，分日告祭太廟、社稷、嶽鎮海瀆及天下名山大川，復告祀天地於圜丘。

translations.literal: In year 9, because the princes were about to depart to their fiefs, on successive days announcements and sacrifices were made at the Grand Ancestral Temple, state and grain altars, peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers, and famous mountains and great rivers under Heaven; Heaven and Earth were again announced at the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 9, as the princes prepared to leave for their fiefs, sacrifices were announced over successive days at the Grand Ancestral Temple, the state and grain altars, the peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers, and famous mountains and rivers throughout the realm, and Heaven and Earth were again announced at the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 初，諸王來朝還籓，祭真武等神於端門，用豕九、羊九、制帛等物，祭護衛旗纛於承天門，亦如之。

translations.literal: At first, when princes came to court and returned to their fiefs, they sacrificed to the True Warrior and other spirits at Duān Gate, using nine pigs, nine sheep, regulated silk, and other offerings; they sacrificed to the protective banners and standards at Chengtian Gate in the same way.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when princes paid court and returned to their domains, they sacrificed to the True Warrior and other spirits at Duān Gate with nine pigs, nine sheep, and regulated silks; they did the same for protective banners and standards at Chengtian Gate.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，帝以其禮太繁，定制豕一、羊一，不用帛。

translations.literal: In year 26 the emperor, finding the ritual too elaborate, fixed it at one pig and one sheep, with no use of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 26 the emperor judged the ritual overly elaborate and fixed it at one pig and one sheep, dispensing with silk.

sentences.zh: 尋又罷端門祭，惟用葷素二壇祭於承天門外。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the sacrifice at Duān Gate was abolished; only two altars, one with meat and one vegetarian, were used for sacrifice outside Chengtian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Duān Gate sacrifice was abolished; only two altars—one with meat offerings and one vegetarian—were kept for sacrifice outside Chengtian Gate.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年，巡狩北京，祭告天地、宗廟、社稷，嘉靖八年秋，以躬祭山川諸神，命先期不必遣官告太廟。

translations.literal: In Yongle 7, on an imperial tour to Beijing, Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and state and grain altars were announced. In the autumn of Jiajing 8, because the emperor personally sacrificed to the mountains, rivers, and other spirits, he ordered that in the preliminary period it was no longer necessary to dispatch officials to announce at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 7, during the imperial tour of Beijing, announcements were made to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the state and grain altars. In the autumn of Jiajing 8, because the emperor intended to sacrifice in person to mountains, rivers, and other spirits, he ordered that officials no longer needed to be dispatched beforehand to announce at the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 凡出入，必親告祖考於內殿。

translations.literal: Whenever going out or returning, one had always to announce in person to ancestral forebears in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever leaving or returning, the emperor always announced in person to his forebears in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 聖誕前一日，以酒果告列聖帝后於奉先殿，至日，以酒脯告皇天上帝於玄極寶殿，遣官以牲醴祭神烈、天壽、純德諸陵山，及東嶽、都城隍，以素羞祭真武及靈濟宮，又告修齋於道極七寶帝尊。

translations.literal: On the day before the imperial birthday, wine and fruit were used to announce to the successive sage emperors and empresses at Fengxian Hall; on the day itself, wine and dried meat were used to announce to the Supreme Lord of Imperial Heaven at the Hall of the Mysterious Pole and Precious Canopy; officials were dispatched with sacrificial animals and wine to sacrifice at the Spirit Splendor, Heavenly Longevity, Pure Virtue, and other imperial tombs and mountains, and at the Eastern Peak and the capital city god; vegetarian offerings were used to sacrifice to the True Warrior and at Lingji Palace; and a report was also made to conduct fasting rites at the Seven Treasures Imperial Lords of the Dao at the Hall of the Utmost Dao.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the imperial birthday, wine and fruit were offered in announcement to successive sage emperors and empresses at Fengxian Hall; on the day itself, wine and dried meat were offered to the Supreme Lord of Imperial Heaven at the Hall of the Mysterious Pole and Precious Canopy. Envoys were sent with sacrificial animals and wine to the Spirit Splendor, Heavenly Longevity, Pure Virtue, and other imperial tomb mountains, as well as the Eastern Peak and the capital city god; vegetarian offerings were sent to the True Warrior and Lingji Palace; and fasting rites were announced at the Seven Treasures Imperial Lords of the Dao.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年，以親祭朝日壇，預告奉先、弘孝、神霄殿。

translations.literal: In Longqing 3, because the emperor personally sacrificed at the Morning Sun altar, advance announcements were made at Fengxian, Hongxiao, and Shenxiao Halls.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 3, in preparation for the emperor's personal sacrifice at the Morning Sun altar, advance announcements were made at Fengxian, Hongxiao, and Shenxiao halls.

sentences.zh: ○祈報

translations.literal: ● Prayer and report
translations.idiomatic: Prayer and Report

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，太祖以春久不雨，祈告諸神祇。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 2 the Taizu, because spring long lacked rain, prayed and announced to the various spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2, when spring brought no rain for a long time, the Taizu prayed to the various spirits.

sentences.zh: 中設風雲雷雨、嶽鎮海瀆，凡五壇。

translations.literal: In the center were set up wind, clouds, thunder, and rain; peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers—in all five altars.
translations.idiomatic: In the center stood five altars: wind, clouds, thunder, and rain; and the peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers.

sentences.zh: 東設鐘山、兩淮、江西、兩廣、海南北、山東、燕南燕薊山川、旗纛諸神，凡七罈。

translations.literal: To the east were set up Zhong Mountain; the Two Huai, Jiangxi, the Two Guangs, Hainan and Haibei, Shandong, Yannan and Yanji mountains and rivers; and spirits of banners and standards—in all seven altars.
translations.idiomatic: To the east stood seven altars: Zhong Mountain; mountains and rivers of the Two Huai, Jiangxi, the Two Guangs, Hainan and Haibei, Shandong, and Yannan and Yanji; and spirits of banners and standards.

sentences.zh: 西設江東、兩浙、福建、湖廣荊襄、河南北、河東、華州山川、京都城隍，凡六壇。

translations.literal: To the west were set up Jiangdong, the Two Zhes, Fujian, Huguang and Jingxiang, Henan and Hebei, Hedong, Huazhou mountains and rivers, and the capital city god—in all six altars.
translations.idiomatic: To the west stood six altars: Jiangdong; mountains and rivers of the Two Zhes, Fujian, Huguang and Jingxiang, Henan and Hebei, Hedong, and Huazhou; and the capital city god.

sentences.zh: 中五壇奠帛。

translations.literal: On the five central altars silk was laid as offering.
translations.idiomatic: Silk offerings were laid on the five central altars.

sentences.zh: 初獻，帝親行禮，兩廡命官分獻。

translations.literal: At the first offering the emperor performed the rite in person; officials in the two side halls performed divided offerings.
translations.idiomatic: At the first oblation the emperor performed the rite in person, while officials in the two side halls made the divided offerings.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，旱。

translations.literal: In the third year, summer: drought.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3, during summer, drought struck.

sentences.zh: 六月朔，帝素服草履，步禱于山川壇。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, the emperor wore plain dress and straw sandals and walked in prayer at the Mountains and Rivers Altar.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month, the emperor put on plain clothes and straw sandals and walked in prayer to the Mountains and Rivers Altar.

sentences.zh: 藁席露坐，晝曝於日，夜臥於地，凡三日。

translations.literal: On a straw mat he sat in the open air; by day he exposed himself to the sun, by night he lay upon the ground—for three days in all.
translations.idiomatic: He sat on a straw mat in the open, exposed himself to the sun by day and slept on the ground at night—for three days.

sentences.zh: 六年，從禮部尚書牛諒言，太歲諸神，春祈秋報，凡十五壇。

translations.literal: In year 6, following Minister of Rites Niu Liang's proposal, for the Great Year and other spirits, spring prayer and autumn report used altogether fifteen altars.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 6, following Minister of Rites Niu Liang's proposal, spring prayer and autumn report to the Great Year and associated spirits required fifteen altars.

sentences.zh: 中，太歲、風雲雷雨、五嶽、五鎮、四海。

translations.literal: In the center: Great Year, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, the Five Peaks, the Five Garrisons, and the Four Seas.
translations.idiomatic: In the center: Great Year; wind, clouds, thunder, and rain; the Five Peaks; the Five Garrisons; and the Four Seas.

sentences.zh: 東，四瀆、京畿山川，春秋二季月將，京都各府城隍。

translations.literal: To the east: the Four Rivers, capital region mountains and rivers, the spring and autumn seasonal monthly generals, and city gods of each capital prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: To the east: the Four Rivers; capital region mountains and rivers; the spring and autumn monthly generals; and city gods of each capital prefecture.

sentences.zh: 西，鐘山、甘肅山川，夏冬二季月將，旗纛戰船等神。

translations.literal: To the west: Zhong Mountain, Gansu mountains and rivers, the summer and winter seasonal monthly generals, and spirits of banners, standards, and warships.
translations.idiomatic: To the west: Zhong Mountain; Gansu mountains and rivers; the summer and winter monthly generals; and spirits of banners, standards, and warships.

sentences.zh: 各五壇。

translations.literal: Five altars each.
translations.idiomatic: Each group comprised five altars.

sentences.zh: 時甘肅新附，故附其山川之祭於京師。

translations.literal: At that time Gansu had newly submitted, so its mountains and rivers sacrifice was attached to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gansu had only recently submitted, its mountains and rivers were included in the capital rites.

sentences.zh: 其親祀之儀與祭告同。

translations.literal: The protocol for personal sacrifice was the same as for sacrificial announcements.
translations.idiomatic: The protocol when the emperor sacrificed in person matched that for sacrificial announcements.

sentences.zh: 正統九年三月，雨雪愆期，遣官祭天地、社稷、太歲、風雲雷雨、嶽鎮海瀆。

translations.literal: In the third month of Zhengtong 9, when snow and rain missed their season, officials were dispatched to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, state and grain altars, Great Year, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, and peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhengtong 9, when rain and snow failed to come on schedule, officials were dispatched to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, the state and grain altars, the Great Year, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, and the peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers.

sentences.zh: 弘治十七年，畿內、山東久旱，命官祭告天壽山，分命各巡撫祭告北嶽、北鎮、東嶽、東鎮、東海。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi 17, when the capital region and Shandong suffered prolonged drought, officials were ordered to announce at Heavenly Longevity Mountain, and each grand coordinator was separately ordered to announce at the Northern Peak, Northern Garrison, Eastern Peak, Eastern Garrison, and Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 17, after prolonged drought in the capital region and Shandong, officials were sent to announce at Heavenly Longevity Mountain, and each grand coordinator was separately ordered to announce at the Northern Peak, Northern Garrison, Eastern Peak, Eastern Garrison, and Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年春，帝諭禮部：「去冬少雪，今當東作，雨澤不降，當親祭南郊社稷、山川。

translations.literal: In the spring of Jiajing 8 the emperor instructed the Ministry of Rites: "Last winter saw little snow; now the eastern ploughing season has come, yet rain and grace have not descended—I should personally sacrifice at the southern suburbs to the state and grain altars and to the mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Jiajing 8 the emperor instructed the Ministry of Rites: "Last winter brought little snow; the eastern ploughing season is at hand, yet rain has not come—I should personally sacrifice at the southern suburbs to the state and grain altars and to the mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 」尚書方獻夫等言： 「《周禮·大宗伯》：『以荒禮哀兇札。

translations.literal: " Minister of Rites Fang Xianfu and others said: "In the 《Rites of Zhou · Grand Minister of Rites》: 'With the rites of desolation one mourns calamity and plague.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Rites Fang Xianfu and others replied: "The 《Rites of Zhou · Grand Minister of Rites》 states: 'With the rites of desolation one mourns calamity and plague.

sentences.zh: 』釋者謂：『君膳不舉，馳道不除，祭事不縣，皆所以示貶損之意。

translations.literal: ' Commentators say: 'The ruler's meals are not served, imperial roads are not cleared, sacrificial music is not suspended—all to show intent of self-diminishment.
translations.idiomatic: ' Commentators explain: 'The ruler's meals are not served, imperial roads are not cleared, sacrificial music is not hung—all to show deliberate self-diminishment.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：『國有大故，則旅上帝及四望。

translations.literal: " It also says: 'When the state has a great cause, then present offerings to the Supreme Lord and the Four Outlooks.
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: 'When the state faces a great emergency, offerings are presented to the Supreme Lord and the Four Outlooks.

sentences.zh: 』釋者曰： 『故謂兇災。

translations.literal: ' Commentators say: 'Cause means disaster and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: ' Commentators explain: 'Cause means disaster and calamity.

sentences.zh: 旅，陳也，陳其祭祀以禱焉，禮不若祀之備也。

translations.literal: Present means to array; array the sacrifices and pray thereby—the rite is not as complete as a full sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: 'Present' means to array; the sacrifices are arrayed and prayer is made thereby—the rite is less complete than a full sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 』今陛下閔勞萬姓，親出祈禱。

translations.literal: ' Now Your Majesty, pitying the labors of the myriad people, goes out in person to pray.
translations.idiomatic: ' Now Your Majesty, pitying the toil of the common people, goes out in person to pray.

sentences.zh: 禮儀務簡約，以答天戒。

translations.literal: The ritual should be kept simple, to answer Heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual should be kept simple, in response to Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 常朝官並從，同致省愆祈籲之誠。

translations.literal: All regular court officials should follow, together expressing sincerity of self-examination and prayerful appeal.
translations.idiomatic: All regular court officials should accompany you, together showing sincerity in self-examination and earnest prayer.

sentences.zh: 」隨具上儀注。

translations.literal: " They then submitted the full protocol.
translations.idiomatic: " They then submitted the full protocol in memorial.

sentences.zh: 二月，親禱南郊，山川同日，社稷用次日，不除道，冠服淺色，羣臣同。

translations.literal: In the second month he prayed in person at the southern suburbs; mountains and rivers on the same day, state and grain altars on the next day; imperial roads were not cleared; caps and garments were in pale colors; all ministers the same.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he prayed in person at the southern suburbs—mountains and rivers on the same day, state and grain altars the next. Imperial roads were not cleared; caps and garments were pale; all ministers dressed likewise.

sentences.zh: 文五品、武四品以上於大祀門外，餘官於南天門外，就班陪祀。

translations.literal: Civil officials of the fifth rank and above and military officials of the fourth rank and above stood outside the Great Sacrifice Gate; the remaining officials stood outside the Southern Heavenly Gate, taking their places to attend the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of fifth rank and above and military officials of fourth rank and above stood outside the Great Sacrifice Gate; other officials stood outside the Southern Heavenly Gate to take their places as attendant sacrificers.

sentences.zh: 是秋，帝欲親祀山川諸神。

translations.literal: That autumn the emperor wished to sacrifice in person to the mountains, rivers, and other spirits.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the emperor wished to sacrifice in person to mountains, rivers, and other spirits.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書李時言：「舊例山川等祭，中夜行禮，先一日出郊齋宿。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Li Shi said: "Under the old precedent, sacrifice to mountains, rivers, and the like was performed at midnight, with fasting and lodging in the suburbs on the preceding day.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Li Shi said: "Under the old precedent, sacrifice to mountains and rivers was performed at midnight, with fasting and lodging in the suburbs on the preceding day.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，清晨迴鑾，兩日畢事，禮太重。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was finished, the imperial procession returned at dawn; the whole affair took two days—the ritual was too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice was finished, the imperial procession returned at dawn; the whole affair took two days—the burden was too great.

sentences.zh: 宜比先農壇例，昧爽行禮。

translations.literal: It would be better to follow the precedent of the Former Agriculture altar and perform the rite at daybreak.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to follow the Former Agriculture altar precedent and perform the rite at daybreak.

sentences.zh: 」因具儀以進。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the full protocol was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " The full protocol was then submitted in memorial.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The order was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 祭服用皮弁，迎神、送神各兩拜。

translations.literal: Sacrificial dress was the skin cap; for welcoming and sending off the spirits, two bows each.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial dress was the skin cap; welcoming and sending off the spirits each required two bows.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大學士李時等以聖嗣未降，請廷臣詣嶽鎮名山祝禱。

translations.literal: In year 11 Grand Secretaries Li Shi and others, because no imperial heir had yet been born, requested that court ministers go to famous peaks and garrisons to offer prayers.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 11 Grand Secretaries Li Shi and others, because no heir had yet been born, requested that court ministers go to famous peaks and garrisons to offer prayers.

sentences.zh: 帝欲分遣道士齎香帛行，令所在守臣行禮，在廷大臣分詣地祇壇祈告。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to dispatch Daoist priests bearing incense and silk separately, ordering local officials to perform the rites, while ministers at court would separately go to the Earthly Powers altar to pray and announce.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to dispatch Daoist priests bearing incense and silk, ordering local officials to perform the rites, while ministers at court would separately pray at the Earthly Powers altar.

sentences.zh: 於是禮部尚書夏言言：「我朝建地祇壇，自嶽鎮海瀆以及遠近名山大川，莫不懷柔，即此而禱，正合古人望衍之義。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minister of Rites Xia Yan said: "Our dynasty established the Earthly Powers altar—from peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers to famous mountains and great rivers near and far, none were left unembraced; to pray here accords with the ancient meaning of expansive outlook.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Xia Yan then said: "Our dynasty established the Earthly Powers altar—from peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers to famous mountains and great rivers near and far, all were embraced; to pray here accords with the ancient meaning of expansive outlook.

sentences.zh: 但輔臣所請，止於嶽鎮。

translations.literal: But what the chief ministers requested stopped at peaks and garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: But what the chief ministers requested covered only peaks and garrisons.

sentences.zh: 竊以山川海瀆，發祥效靈，與嶽鎮同功，況基運、翊聖、神烈、天壽、純德諸山，又祖宗妥靈之地，祈禱之禮，皆不可缺。

translations.literal: I venture to hold that mountains, rivers, seas, and rivers, in issuing blessings and showing efficacy, share the same merit as peaks and garrisons; moreover the mountains of Foundation of Fortune, Aid to Sagacity, Spirit Splendor, Heavenly Longevity, and Pure Virtue are also places where the imperial ancestors rest in spirit—prayer rites for all cannot be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that mountains, rivers, seas, and streams, in issuing blessings and showing efficacy, share the same merit as peaks and garrisons; moreover the Foundation of Fortune, Aid to Sagacity, Spirit Splendor, Heavenly Longevity, and Pure Virtue mountains are also where imperial ancestors rest in spirit—prayer rites for all cannot be omitted.

sentences.zh: 」遂命大臣詣壇分祀。

translations.literal: " Thereupon ministers were ordered to go to the altar and perform divided sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: " Ministers were then ordered to go to the altar and perform divided sacrifices.

sentences.zh: ○神祇壇

translations.literal: ● Altar of spirits
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Altars

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，從禮部尚書崔亮言，建天下神祇壇於圓丘壝外之東，及方丘壝外之西。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 2, following Minister of Rites Cui Liang's proposal, the Altar of Spirits Under Heaven was built east outside the Circular Mound enclosure and west outside the Square Mound enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2, following Minister of Rites Cui Liang's proposal, the Altar of Spirits Under Heaven was built east of the Circular Mound enclosure and west of the Square Mound enclosure.

sentences.zh: 郊祀前期，帝躬詣壇，設神位，西向，以酒脯祭告。

translations.literal: In the preliminary period of the suburban sacrifice, the emperor went in person to the altar, set up spirit seats facing west, and announced with wine and dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: Before the suburban sacrifice, the emperor went in person to the altar, set up spirit seats facing west, and announced with wine and dried meat.

sentences.zh: 郊之日，俟分獻從祀將畢，就壇以祭。

translations.literal: On the day of the suburban sacrifice, when the divided offerings and attendant sacrifices were nearly finished, he went to the altar to sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the suburban sacrifice, when the divided offerings and attendant sacrifices were nearly finished, he went to the altar to perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 後定遣官預告。

translations.literal: Later it was fixed that officials should be dispatched for advance announcement.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was fixed that officials would be dispatched for advance announcement.

sentences.zh: 又建山川壇於正陽門外天地壇西，合祀諸神。

translations.literal: A Mountains and Rivers Altar was also built west of the Heaven and Earth altar outside Zhengyang Gate, combining sacrifice to the various spirits.
translations.idiomatic: A Mountains and Rivers Altar was also built west of the Heaven and Earth altar outside Zhengyang Gate, combining sacrifice to the various spirits.

sentences.zh: 凡設壇十有九，太歲、春夏秋冬四季月將爲第一，次風雲雷雨，次五嶽，次五鎮，次四海，次四瀆，次京都鐘山，次江東，次江西，次湖廣，次淮東、淮西，次浙東、浙西、福建，次廣東、廣西、海南、海北，次山東、山西、河南、河北，次北平、陝西，次左江、右江，次安南、高麗、占城諸國山川，次京都城隍，次六纛大神、旗纛大將、五方旗神、戰船、金鼓、銃砲、弓弩、飛槍飛石、陣前陣後諸神，皆躬自行禮。

translations.literal: In all nineteen altars were set up: Great Year and the spring, summer, autumn, and winter seasonal monthly generals first; next wind, clouds, thunder, and rain; next the Five Peaks; next the Five Garrisons; next the Four Seas; next the Four Rivers; next the capital Zhong Mountain; next Jiangdong; next Jiangxi; next Huguang; next Huaidong and Huaidi; next Zhedong, Zhexi, and Fujian; next Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, and Haibei; next Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, and Hebei; next Beiping and Shaanxi; next Zuojiang and Youjiang; next mountains and rivers of Annam, Goryeo, Champa, and other states; next the capital city god; next the Six Banners Great Spirit, Banner and Standard Great General, Five Directions Banner Spirits, warships, gongs and drums, cannon, bows and crossbows, flying spears and flying stones, and spirits before and behind the battle array—all performed by the emperor in person.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen altars were set up in all: first Great Year and the spring, summer, autumn, and winter monthly generals; then wind, clouds, thunder, and rain; the Five Peaks; the Five Garrisons; the Four Seas; the Four Rivers; the capital Zhong Mountain; Jiangdong; Jiangxi; Huguang; Huaidong and Huaidi; Zhedong, Zhexi, and Fujian; Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, and Haibei; Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, and Hebei; Beiping and Shaanxi; Zuojiang and Youjiang; mountains and rivers of Annam, Goryeo, Champa, and other states; the capital city god; and the Six Banners Great Spirit, Banner and Standard Great General, Five Directions Banner Spirits, warships, gongs and drums, cannon, bows and crossbows, flying spears and flying stones, and spirits before and behind the battle array—all performed by the emperor in person.

sentences.zh: 先祭，禮官奏：「祝文，太歲以下至四海，凡五壇，稱臣者親署御名。

translations.literal: Before the sacrifice, ritual officials reported: "In the prayer text, from Great Year down to the Four Seas—in all five altars—where the text says 'your subject,' the emperor should personally sign the imperial name.
translations.idiomatic: Before the sacrifice, ritual officials reported: "In the prayer text, from Great Year down to the Four Seas—in all five altars—where the text says 'your subject,' the emperor should personally sign his imperial name.

sentences.zh: 其鐘山諸神，稱餘者請令禮官代署。

translations.literal: For Zhong Mountain and the other spirits, where the text says 'I, the remainder,' please allow ritual officials to sign on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: For Zhong Mountain and the other spirits, where the text says 'I, the remainder,' please allow ritual officials to sign on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朋友書牘，尚親題姓名，況神明乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Even in letters to friends one still personally writes one's name—how much more so for the spirits?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "Even in letters to friends one still personally writes one's name—how much more so for the spirits?

sentences.zh: 」遂加親署。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he added his personal signature.
translations.idiomatic: " He then added his personal signature.

sentences.zh: 後又定驚蟄、秋分後三日，遣官祭山川壇諸神。

translations.literal: Later it was also fixed that three days after Awakening of Insects and three days after the autumn equinox, officials should be dispatched to sacrifice to the spirits at the Mountains and Rivers Altar.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was also fixed that three days after Awakening of Insects and three days after the autumn equinox, officials would be dispatched to sacrifice to the spirits at the Mountains and Rivers Altar.

sentences.zh: 七年令春、秋仲月上旬，擇日以祭。

translations.literal: In year 7 an order was issued that in the first ten-day period of the second and eighth months of spring and autumn, an auspicious day should be chosen for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 7 an order was issued that in the first ten-day period of the second and eighth months of spring and autumn, an auspicious day should be chosen for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 九年，復定山川壇制，凡十三壇。

translations.literal: In year 9 the Mountains and Rivers Altar system was again fixed, with thirteen altars in all.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 9 the Mountains and Rivers Altar system was again fixed, with thirteen altars in all.

sentences.zh: 正殿，太歲、風雲雷雨、五嶽、五鎮、四海、四瀆、鐘山七罈。

translations.literal: In the main hall: Great Year, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, the Five Peaks, the Five Garrisons, the Four Seas, the Four Rivers, and Zhong Mountain—in all seven altars.
translations.idiomatic: In the main hall stood seven altars: Great Year; wind, clouds, thunder, and rain; the Five Peaks; the Five Garrisons; the Four Seas; the Four Rivers; and Zhong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 東西廡各三壇，東，京畿山川、夏冬二季月將。

translations.literal: East and west side halls each had three altars; to the east: capital region mountains and rivers and the summer and winter seasonal monthly generals.
translations.idiomatic: East and west side halls each had three altars; to the east: capital region mountains and rivers and the summer and winter monthly generals.

sentences.zh: 西，春秋二季月將、京都城隍。

translations.literal: To the west: the spring and autumn seasonal monthly generals and the capital city god.
translations.idiomatic: To the west: the spring and autumn monthly generals and the capital city god.

sentences.zh: 十年，定正殿七罈，帝親行禮，東西廡遣功臣分獻。

translations.literal: In year 10 the seven altars of the main hall were fixed; the emperor performed the rite in person, while meritorious officials in the east and west side halls performed divided offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 10 the seven main-hall altars were fixed; the emperor performed the rite in person, while meritorious officials in the east and west side halls made the divided offerings.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，增修大祀殿諸神壇壝。

translations.literal: In year 21 the spirit altars and enclosures of the Great Sacrifice Hall were enlarged and repaired.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 21 the spirit altars and enclosures of the Great Sacrifice Hall were enlarged and repaired.

sentences.zh: 乃敕十三壇諸神並停春祭，每歲八月中旬，擇日祭之。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued that the spirits of the thirteen altars should all suspend spring sacrifice; each year in the middle ten-day period of the eighth month an auspicious day was chosen for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then suspended spring sacrifice for the spirits of all thirteen altars; each year in the middle ten-day period of the eighth month an auspicious day was chosen for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 命禮部更定祭山川壇儀，與社稷同。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites was ordered to revise the Mountains and Rivers Altar ritual, making it the same as for the state and grain altars.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites was ordered to revise the Mountains and Rivers Altar ritual to match that of the state and grain altars.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，京師建山川壇，並同南京制，惟正殿鐘山之右，益以天壽山之神。

translations.literal: During the Yongle period a Mountains and Rivers Altar was built in the capital on the same model as Nanjing, except that to the right of Zhong Mountain in the main hall the spirit of Heavenly Longevity Mountain was added.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle period a Mountains and Rivers Altar was built in the capital on the Nanjing model, except that to the right of Zhong Mountain in the main hall the spirit of Heavenly Longevity Mountain was added.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年，改山川壇名爲天神地祇壇，改序雲師、雨師、風伯、雷師。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 11 the Mountains and Rivers Altar was renamed the Altar of Heavenly Spirits and Earthly Powers, and the order was changed to Master of Clouds, Master of Rain, Earl of Wind, and Master of Thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 11 the Mountains and Rivers Altar was renamed the Altar of Heavenly Spirits and Earthly Powers, and the order was changed to Master of Clouds, Master of Rain, Earl of Wind, and Master of Thunder.

sentences.zh: 天神壇在左，南向，雲、雨、雷，凡四壇。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Spirits altar was on the left, facing south: cloud, rain, and thunder—in all four altars.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Spirits altar stood on the left, facing south: cloud, rain, wind, and thunder—in all four altars.

sentences.zh: 地祇壇在右，北向，五嶽、五鎮、基運翊聖神烈天壽純德五陵山、四海、四瀆，凡五壇。

translations.literal: The Earthly Powers altar was on the right, facing north: the Five Peaks, Five Garrisons, mountains of Foundation of Fortune, Aid to Sagacity, Spirit Splendor, Heavenly Longevity, and Pure Virtue, the Four Seas, and the Four Rivers—in all five altars.
translations.idiomatic: The Earthly Powers altar stood on the right, facing north: the Five Peaks; Five Garrisons; Foundation of Fortune, Aid to Sagacity, Spirit Splendor, Heavenly Longevity, and Pure Virtue mountains; the Four Seas; and the Four Rivers—in all five altars.

sentences.zh: 從祀，京畿山川，西向；

translations.literal: As attendant sacrifice: capital region mountains and rivers, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: As attendant sacrifices: capital region mountains and rivers faced west;

sentences.zh: 天下山川，東向。

translations.literal: mountains and rivers under Heaven, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: mountains and rivers throughout the realm, facing east.

sentences.zh: 以辰、戌、醜、未年仲秋，皇帝親祭，餘年遣大臣攝祭。

translations.literal: In the mid-autumn of years Chen, Xu, Chou, and Wei the emperor sacrificed in person; in other years great ministers performed the rite as his proxy.
translations.idiomatic: In the mid-autumn of Chen, Xu, Chou, and Wei years the emperor sacrificed in person; in other years great ministers performed the rite as his proxy.

sentences.zh: 其太歲、月將、旗纛、城隍，別祀之。

translations.literal: Great Year, monthly generals, banners and standards, and city gods were sacrificed to separately.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Year, monthly generals, banners and standards, and city gods received separate sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十七年，加上皇天上帝尊稱，預告於神祇，遂設壇於圜丘外壝東南，親定神祇壇位，陳設儀式。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the honorific title of the Supreme Lord of Imperial Heaven was added, advance announcement was made to the spirits, and an altar was thereupon set up southeast of the Circular Mound's outer enclosure; the emperor personally fixed the spirit altar seats and arranged the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 17 the honorific title of the Supreme Lord of Imperial Heaven was added, advance announcement was made to the spirits, and an altar was set up southeast of the Circular Mound's outer enclosure; the emperor personally fixed the spirit altar seats and arranged the ritual.

sentences.zh: 禮部言：「皇上親獻大明壇，則四壇分獻諸臣，不敢並列。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said: "When Your Majesty personally offers at the Great Brightness altar, the ministers performing divided offerings at the four altars dare not stand alongside.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites said: "When Your Majesty personally offers at the Great Brightness altar, the ministers performing divided offerings at the four altars dare not stand alongside.

sentences.zh: 請先上香畢，命官代獻。

translations.literal: We ask that incense be offered first and completed, then that officials be ordered to offer in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that incense be offered first and completed, then that officials be ordered to offer in his stead.

sentences.zh: 」帝裁定，上香、奠帛、獻爵復位後，分獻官方行禮。

translations.literal: " The emperor decided: after incense offering, silk presentation, and cup offering and returning to position, the ministers performing divided offerings would then perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor decided that after incense offering, silk presentation, and cup offering and returning to position, the ministers performing divided offerings would then perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 亞、終二獻，執事官代，餘壇俱獻官三行。

translations.literal: For the second and final offerings, attending officials substituted; at the remaining altars all offering officials proceeded in three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: For the second and final offerings, attending officials substituted; at the remaining altars all offering officials proceeded in three ranks.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，禮臣言：「天神地祇已從祀南北郊，其仲秋神祇之祭不宜復舉。

translations.literal: In Longqing 1, ritual officials said: "Heavenly spirits and earthly powers already accompany sacrifice at the northern and southern suburbs; the mid-autumn sacrifice to spirits should not be performed again.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 1, ritual officials said: "Heavenly spirits and earthly powers already accompany sacrifice at the northern and southern suburbs; the mid-autumn sacrifice to spirits should not be performed again.

sentences.zh: 」令罷之。

translations.literal: " An order was issued to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: " An order was issued to abolish it.

sentences.zh: ○星辰壇

translations.literal: ● Stars and constellations altar
translations.idiomatic: Stars and Constellations Altar

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，帝謂中書省臣：「日月皆專壇祭，而星辰乃祔祭於月壇，非禮也。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 3 the emperor told members of the Secretariat: "Sun and moon each have dedicated altar sacrifice, yet the stars and constellations are offered in collateral sacrifice at the moon altar—this is not ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 the emperor told members of the Secretariat: "Sun and moon each have dedicated altar sacrifice, yet the stars and constellations are offered in collateral sacrifice at the moon altar—this is not ritual.

sentences.zh: 」禮部擬於城南諸神享祭壇正南向，增九間，朝日夕月祭周天星辰，俱於是行禮。

translations.literal: " The Ministry of Rites proposed adding nine bays to the southern suburb Altar of Sacrifice to All Spirits, facing directly south; sacrifice to the morning sun, evening moon, and all stars of heaven would all be performed there.
translations.idiomatic: " The Ministry of Rites proposed adding nine bays to the southern suburb Altar of Sacrifice to All Spirits, facing directly south; sacrifice to the morning sun, evening moon, and all stars of heaven would all be performed there.

sentences.zh: 朝日夕月仍以春秋分祭，星辰則於天壽節前三日。

translations.literal: Morning sun and evening moon would still be sacrificed at the spring and autumn equinoxes; the stars and constellations on the three days before the Heavenly Longevity Festival.
translations.idiomatic: Morning sun and evening moon would still be sacrificed at the spring and autumn equinoxes; the stars and constellations on the three days before the Heavenly Longevity Festival.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，帝躬祀周天星辰。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year the emperor personally sacrificed to all stars of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Hongwu 4 the emperor personally sacrificed to all stars of heaven.

sentences.zh: 正殿共十壇，中設周天星辰位，儀如朝日。

translations.literal: The main hall had ten altars in all; at the center was placed the seat for all stars of heaven; the ritual was as for the morning sun.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall had ten altars in all; at the center was placed the seat for all stars of heaven; the ritual was as for the morning sun.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以星辰既從祀南郊，罷禜星之祭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, because the stars and constellations already accompanied sacrifice at the southern suburb, the Star Lustration sacrifice was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 21, because the stars and constellations already accompanied sacrifice at the southern suburb, the Star Lustration sacrifice was abolished.

sentences.zh: ○靈星諸神

translations.literal: ● Spirit Star and various spirits
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Star and Associated Deities

sentences.zh: ○太歲月將風雲雷雨之祀

translations.literal: ● Sacrifice to the Great Year, monthly generals, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the Great Year, Monthly Generals, Wind, Clouds, Thunder, and Rain

sentences.zh: 古無太歲、月將壇宇之制，明始重其祭。

translations.literal: Antiquity had no institution of altars and halls for the Great Year and monthly generals; the Ming first gave weight to their sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity had no institution of altars and halls for the Great Year and monthly generals; the Ming first gave weight to their sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 增雲師於風師之次，亦自明始。

translations.literal: Adding the Master of Clouds after the Master of Wind also began with the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Adding the Master of Clouds after the Master of Wind also began with the Ming.

sentences.zh: 太祖既以太歲諸神從祀圜丘，又合祭羣祀壇。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, having already made the Great Year and associated spirits attendant sacrifices at the Circular Mound, also combined sacrifice at the Altar of Collective Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor, having already made the Great Year and associated spirits attendant sacrifices at the Circular Mound, also combined sacrifice at the Altar of Collective Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 已而命禮官議專祀壇壝。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he ordered ritual officials to consider dedicated altars and enclosures.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he ordered ritual officials to consider dedicated altars and enclosures.

sentences.zh: 禮臣言：「太歲者，十二辰之神。

translations.literal: Ritual officials said: "The Great Year is the spirit of the twelve earthly branches.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials said: "The Great Year is the spirit of the twelve earthly branches.

sentences.zh: 按《說文》，歲字從步從戌。

translations.literal: According to the Explaining Graphs, the character for 'year' combines 'step' with 'xu.'
translations.idiomatic: According to the Explaining Graphs, the character for 'year' combines 'step' with 'xu.'

sentences.zh: 木星一歲行一次，歷十二辰而周天，若步然也。

translations.literal: Jupiter in one year traverses one station, passing through the twelve earthly branches to complete the circuit of heaven—as if stepping.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter in one year traverses one station, passing through the twelve earthly branches to complete the circuit of heaven—as if stepping.

sentences.zh: 陰陽家說，又有十二月將，十日十二時所直之神，若天乙、天罡、太乙、功曹、太沖之類。

translations.literal: In yin-yang theory there are also the twelve monthly generals and the spirits presiding over the ten days and twelve hours—such as Heavenly Yi, Heavenly Gang, Grand Unity, Merit Clerk, Grand Surge, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In yin-yang theory there are also the twelve monthly generals and the spirits presiding over the ten days and twelve hours—such as Heavenly Yi, Heavenly Gang, Grand Unity, Merit Clerk, Grand Surge, and the like.

sentences.zh: 雖不經見，歷代因之。

translations.literal: Though not found in the canonical texts, successive dynasties retained them.
translations.idiomatic: Though not found in the canonical texts, successive dynasties retained them.

sentences.zh: 元每有大興作，祭太歲、月將、日直、時直於太史院。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan, whenever there were major construction projects, the Great Year, monthly generals, day-presiding and hour-presiding spirits were sacrificed to at the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan, whenever there were major construction projects, the Great Year, monthly generals, day-presiding and hour-presiding spirits were sacrificed to at the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 若風師、雨師之祀，見於《周官》，後世皆有祭。

translations.literal: As for sacrifice to the Master of Wind and Master of Rain, this appears in the Rites of Zhou; later ages all had sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: As for sacrifice to the Master of Wind and Master of Rain, this appears in the Rites of Zhou; later ages all had sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 唐天寶中，增雷師於雨師之次。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era of Tang, the Master of Thunder was added after the Master of Rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era of Tang, the Master of Thunder was added after the Master of Rain.

sentences.zh: 宋、元因之。

translations.literal: Song and Yuan followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Yuan followed this.

sentences.zh: 然唐制各以時別祭，失享祀本意。

translations.literal: Yet under the Tang system each was separately sacrificed according to season, losing the original intent of sacrificial offering.
translations.idiomatic: Yet under the Tang system each was separately sacrificed according to season, losing the original intent of sacrificial offering.

sentences.zh: 宜以太歲、風雲雷雨諸天神合爲一罈，諸地祇爲一罈，春秋專祀。

translations.literal: It is fitting that the Great Year, wind, clouds, thunder, rain, and other heavenly spirits be combined into one altar, and all earthly powers into one altar, with dedicated spring and autumn sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting that the Great Year, wind, clouds, thunder, rain, and other heavenly spirits be combined into one altar, and all earthly powers into one altar, with dedicated spring and autumn sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」乃定驚蟄、秋分日祀太歲諸神於城南。

translations.literal: " Thereupon sacrifice to the Great Year and associated spirits at the southern suburb was fixed for Awakening of Insects and the autumn equinox.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon sacrifice to the Great Year and associated spirits at the southern suburb was fixed for Awakening of Insects and the autumn equinox.

sentences.zh: 三年後以諸神陰陽一氣，流行無間，乃合二壇爲一，而增四季月將。

translations.literal: Three years later, because the various spirits are one qi of yin and yang flowing without interruption, the two altars were combined into one, and the four seasonal monthly generals were added.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, because the various spirits are one qi of yin and yang flowing without interruption, the two altars were combined into one, and the four seasonal monthly generals were added.

sentences.zh: 又改祭期，與地祇俱用驚蟄、秋分後三日。

translations.literal: The sacrificial dates were also changed; together with earthly powers both used the third day after Awakening of Insects and the autumn equinox.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial dates were also changed; together with earthly powers both used the third day after Awakening of Insects and the autumn equinox.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年，命禮部考太歲壇制。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 10 an order was issued for the Ministry of Rites to examine the regulations for the Great Year altar.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 10 an order was issued for the Ministry of Rites to examine the regulations for the Great Year altar.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「太歲之神，唐、宋祀典不載，元雖有祭，亦無常典。

translations.literal: Ritual officials said: "The spirit of the Great Year is not recorded in the Tang and Song sacrificial codes; though the Yuan had sacrifice, there was no fixed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials said: "The spirit of the Great Year is not recorded in the Tang and Song sacrificial codes; though the Yuan had sacrifice, there was no fixed ritual.

sentences.zh: 壇宇之制，於古無稽。

translations.literal: Regulations for altar and hall cannot be verified against antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for altar and hall cannot be verified against antiquity.

sentences.zh: 太歲天神，宜設壇露祭，準社稷壇制而差小。

translations.literal: The Great Year as heavenly spirit should have an open-air altar for sacrifice, modeled on the altars of soil and grain but somewhat smaller.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Year as heavenly spirit should have an open-air altar for sacrifice, modeled on the altars of soil and grain but somewhat smaller.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 遂建太歲壇於正陽門外之西，與天壇對。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Great Year Altar was built west outside the Gate of Correct Yang, facing the Altar of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Great Year Altar was built west outside the Gate of Correct Yang, facing the Altar of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 中，太歲殿。

translations.literal: At the center, the Great Year Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the center, the Great Year Hall.

sentences.zh: 東廡，春、秋月將二壇。

translations.literal: In the east corridor, two altars for the spring and autumn monthly generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the east corridor, two altars for the spring and autumn monthly generals.

sentences.zh: 西廡，夏、冬月將二壇。

translations.literal: In the west corridor, two altars for the summer and winter monthly generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the west corridor, two altars for the summer and winter monthly generals.

sentences.zh: 帝親祭於拜殿中。

translations.literal: The emperor sacrificed in person in the bowing hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sacrificed in person in the bowing hall.

sentences.zh: 每歲孟春享廟，歲暮祫祭之日，遣官致祭。

translations.literal: Each year on the day of spring ancestral offering at the temple and end-of-year unified ancestral offering, officials were dispatched to perform sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Each year on the day of spring ancestral offering at the temple and end-of-year unified ancestral offering, officials were dispatched to perform sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 王國府州縣亦祀風雲雷雨師，仍築壇城西南。

translations.literal: Princely states, prefectures, departments, and counties also sacrificed to the masters of wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, still building altars southwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Princely states, prefectures, departments, and counties also sacrificed to the masters of wind, clouds, thunder, and rain, still building altars southwest of the city.

sentences.zh: 祭用驚蟄、秋分日。

translations.literal: Sacrifice used the days of Awakening of Insects and the autumn equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice used the days of Awakening of Insects and the autumn equinox.

sentences.zh: ○嶽鎮海瀆山川之祀

translations.literal: ● Sacrifice to peaks, garrisons, seas, rivers, mountains, and rivers
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to Peaks, Garrisons, Seas, Rivers, Mountains, and Rivers

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，太祖以嶽瀆諸神合祭城南，未有專祀。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 2 the Founding Emperor, because the spirits of peaks and rivers were jointly sacrificed at the southern suburb, had no dedicated sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2 the Founding Emperor, because the spirits of peaks and rivers were jointly sacrificed at the southern suburb, had no dedicated sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又享祀之所，屋而不壇，非尊神之道。

translations.literal: Moreover the place of sacrificial offering used buildings rather than altars—not the way to honor spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the place of sacrificial offering used buildings rather than altars—not the way to honor spirits.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「虞舜祭四嶽，《王制》始有五嶽之稱。

translations.literal: Ritual officials said: "Emperor Shun of Yu sacrificed to the four peaks; the Wangzhi first gave the title of five peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials said: "Emperor Shun of Yu sacrificed to the four peaks; the Royal Regulations first gave the title of five peaks.

sentences.zh: 《周官》：「兆四望於四郊」，《鄭注》以四望爲五嶽四鎮四瀆。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: 'Establish the four outlooks in the four suburbs'—Zheng's commentary takes the four outlooks as the five peaks, four garrisons, and four rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou: 'Establish the four outlooks in the four suburbs'—Zheng's commentary takes the four outlooks as the five peaks, four garrisons, and four rivers.

sentences.zh: 《詩序》巡狩而禮四嶽河海，則又有四海之祭。

translations.literal: The Preface to the Odes on imperial tours to inspect and rite to the four peaks and river and sea—this adds sacrifice to the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: The Preface to the Odes on imperial tours to inspect and perform rites to the four peaks and river and sea—this adds sacrifice to the four seas.

sentences.zh: 蓋天子方望之事，無所不通。

translations.literal: For the Son of Heaven's business of gazing in the four directions, nothing is not reached.
translations.idiomatic: For the Son of Heaven's business of gazing in the four directions, nothing is not reached.

sentences.zh: 而嶽鎮海瀆，在諸侯封內，則各祀之。

translations.literal: And for the peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers within feudatories' domains, each feudatory sacrificed to its own.
translations.idiomatic: And for the peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers within feudatories' domains, each feudatory sacrificed to its own.

sentences.zh: 奏罷封建，嶽瀆皆領於祠官。

translations.literal: When enfeoffment was abolished by decree, peaks and rivers all came under the charge of sacrificial officials.
translations.idiomatic: When enfeoffment was abolished by decree, peaks and rivers all came under the charge of sacrificial officials.

sentences.zh: 漢復建諸侯，則侯國各祀其封內山川，天子無與。

translations.literal: Han restored feudatories, and each marquisate sacrificed to the mountains and rivers within its domain; the Son of Heaven had no part.
translations.idiomatic: Han restored feudatories, and each marquisate sacrificed to the mountains and rivers within its domain; the Son of Heaven had no part.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，諸侯或分或廢，五嶽皆在天子之邦。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wu's time feudatories were variously divided or abolished, and all five peaks fell within the Son of Heaven's domain.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wu's time feudatories were variously divided or abolished, and all five peaks fell within the Son of Heaven's domain.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，始有使者持節祠嶽瀆之禮。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xuan's time the ritual of dispatching envoys bearing imperial credentials to sacrifice to peaks and rivers first appeared.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xuan's time the ritual of dispatching envoys bearing imperial credentials to sacrifice to peaks and rivers first appeared.

sentences.zh: 由魏及隋，嶽鎮海瀆，即其地立祠，有司致祭。

translations.literal: From Wei through Sui, for the peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers, temples were established on the spot and officials performed sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei through Sui, for the peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers, temples were established on the spot and officials performed sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 唐、宋之制，有命本界刺史、縣令之祀，有因郊祀而望祭之祀，又有遣使之祀。

translations.literal: The Tang and Song systems had sacrifice by order to the prefect and county magistrate of the local jurisdiction, sacrifice by distant gazing at the time of suburban sacrifice, and also sacrificial dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang and Song systems had sacrifice by order to the prefect and county magistrate of the local jurisdiction, sacrifice by distant gazing at the time of suburban sacrifice, and also sacrificial dispatch.

sentences.zh: 元遣使祀嶽鎮海瀆，分東西南北中爲五道。

translations.literal: The Yuan dispatched envoys to sacrifice to peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers, dividing into five routes: east, south, west, north, and center.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan dispatched envoys to sacrifice to peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers, dividing into five routes: east, south, west, north, and center.

sentences.zh: 今宜以嶽鎮海瀆及天下山川城隍諸地祇合爲一罈。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting that peaks, garrisons, seas, rivers, and mountains and rivers and city gods throughout the realm be combined into one altar.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is fitting that peaks, garrisons, seas, rivers, mountains and rivers, and city gods throughout the realm be combined into one altar.

sentences.zh: 與天神埒，春秋專祀。

translations.literal: Matching the heavenly spirits, with dedicated spring and autumn sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On a par with the heavenly spirits, with dedicated spring and autumn sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」遂定祭日以清明霜降。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the sacrificial days were fixed as Pure Brightness and Frost Descent.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the sacrificial days were fixed as Pure Brightness and Frost Descent.

sentences.zh: 前期一日，皇帝躬省牲。

translations.literal: One day beforehand the emperor personally inspected the victims.
translations.idiomatic: One day beforehand the emperor personally inspected the victims.

sentences.zh: 至日，服通天冠絳紗袍，詣嶽鎮海瀆前，行三獻禮。

translations.literal: On the day, wearing the Heaven-Penetrating cap and crimson gauze robe, he proceeded before the peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers and performed the three-offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the day, wearing the Heaven-Penetrating cap and crimson gauze robe, he proceeded before the peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers and performed the three-offering rite.

sentences.zh: 山川城隍，分獻官行禮。

translations.literal: Mountains, rivers, and city gods—ministers performing divided offerings performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains, rivers, and city gods—ministers performing divided offerings performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 是年，命官十八人，祭天下嶽鎮海瀆之神。

translations.literal: That year eighteen officials were appointed to sacrifice to the spirits of all peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That year eighteen officials were appointed to sacrifice to the spirits of all peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers under heaven.

sentences.zh: 帝皮弁御奉天殿，躬署御名，以香祝授使者。

translations.literal: Wearing the leather cap the emperor attended the Hall of Reverence for Heaven, personally signed his imperial name, and conferred the incense prayer upon the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing the leather cap the emperor attended the Hall of Reverence for Heaven, personally signed his imperial name, and conferred the incense prayer upon the envoys.

sentences.zh: 百官公服，送至中書省，使者奉以行。

translations.literal: Officials in full court dress escorted them to the Secretariat; the envoys departed bearing them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in full court dress escorted them to the Secretariat; the envoys departed bearing them.

sentences.zh: 黃金合貯香，黃綺幡二，白金二十五兩市祭物。

translations.literal: Incense was stored in a gold casket; two yellow damask banners; twenty-five taels of white gold to purchase sacrificial items.
translations.idiomatic: Incense was stored in a gold casket; two yellow damask banners; twenty-five taels of white gold to purchase sacrificial items.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔定嶽鎮海瀆神號。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict fixed the spirit titles of the peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 an edict fixed the spirit titles of the peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers.

sentences.zh: 略曰：「爲治之道，必本於禮。

translations.literal: In summary it said: "The way of governing must take root in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In summary it said: "The way of governing must take root in ritual.

sentences.zh: 嶽鎮海瀆之封，起自唐、宋。

translations.literal: Enfeoffment titles for peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers began in Tang and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffment titles for peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers began in Tang and Song.

sentences.zh: 夫英靈之氣，萃而爲神，必受命於上帝，豈國家封號所可加？

translations.literal: Spirits formed when numinous qi gathers—they must receive mandate from the Sovereign on High; how can national enfeoffment titles be added?
translations.idiomatic: Spirits formed when numinous qi gathers—they must receive mandate from the Sovereign on High; how can national enfeoffment titles be added?

sentences.zh: 瀆禮不經，莫此爲甚。

translations.literal: In violation of ritual, nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: In violation of ritual, nothing exceeds this.

sentences.zh: 今依古定制，並去前代所封名號。

translations.literal: Now following ancient regulations, all former enfeoffment titles of former dynasties shall be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Now following ancient regulations, all former enfeoffment titles of former dynasties shall be removed.

sentences.zh: 五嶽稱東嶽泰山之神，南嶽衡山之神，中嶽嵩山之神，西嶽華山之神，北嶽恆山之神。

translations.literal: The five peaks shall be titled Spirit of Mount Tai, Eastern Peak; Spirit of Mount Heng, Southern Peak; Spirit of Mount Song, Central Peak; Spirit of Mount Hua, Western Peak; Spirit of Mount Heng, Northern Peak.
translations.idiomatic: The five peaks shall be titled Spirit of Mount Tai, Eastern Peak; Spirit of Mount Heng, Southern Peak; Spirit of Mount Song, Central Peak; Spirit of Mount Hua, Western Peak; Spirit of Mount Heng, Northern Peak.

sentences.zh: 五鎮稱東鎮沂山之神，南鎮會稽山之神，中鎮霍山之神，西鎮吳山之神，北鎮醫無閭山之神。

translations.literal: The five garrisons shall be titled Spirit of Mount Yi, Eastern Garrison; Spirit of Mount Kuaiji, Southern Garrison; Spirit of Mount Huo, Central Garrison; Spirit of Mount Wu, Western Garrison; Spirit of Mount Yiwulu, Northern Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The five garrisons shall be titled Spirit of Mount Yi, Eastern Garrison; Spirit of Mount Kuaiji, Southern Garrison; Spirit of Mount Huo, Central Garrison; Spirit of Mount Wu, Western Garrison; Spirit of Mount Yiwulu, Northern Garrison.

sentences.zh: 四海稱東海之神，南海之神，西海之神，北海之神。

translations.literal: The four seas shall be titled Spirit of the Eastern Sea; Spirit of the Southern Sea; Spirit of the Western Sea; Spirit of the Northern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: The four seas shall be titled Spirit of the Eastern Sea; Spirit of the Southern Sea; Spirit of the Western Sea; Spirit of the Northern Sea.

sentences.zh: 四瀆稱東瀆大淮之神，南瀆大江之神，西瀆大河之神，北瀆大濟之神。

translations.literal: The four rivers shall be titled Spirit of the Great Huai, Eastern River; Spirit of the Great Yangtze, Southern River; Spirit of the Great Yellow River, Western River; Spirit of the Great Ji, Northern River.
translations.idiomatic: The four rivers shall be titled Spirit of the Great Huai, Eastern River; Spirit of the Great Yangtze, Southern River; Spirit of the Great Yellow River, Western River; Spirit of the Great Ji, Northern River.

sentences.zh: 」帝躬署名於祝文，遣官以更定神號告祭。

translations.literal: " The emperor personally signed the prayer text and dispatched officials to announce and sacrifice with the revised spirit titles.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor personally signed the prayer text and dispatched officials to announce and sacrifice with the revised spirit titles.

sentences.zh: 六年，禮官言：「四川未平，望祭江瀆於峽州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year ritual officials said: "Sichuan is not yet pacified; distant-gazing sacrifice to the rivers was performed at Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 6 ritual officials said: "Sichuan is not yet pacified; distant-gazing sacrifice to the rivers was performed at Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 今蜀既下，當遣人於南瀆致祭。

translations.literal: Now that Shu has fallen, envoys should be sent to perform sacrifice at the Southern River.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Shu has fallen, envoys should be sent to perform sacrifice at the Southern River.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 十年，命官十八人分祀嶽鎮海瀆，賜之制。

translations.literal: In the tenth year eighteen officials were appointed to perform divided sacrifice to peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers; ceremonial robes were conferred upon them.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 10 eighteen officials were appointed to perform divided sacrifice to peaks, garrisons, seas, and rivers; ceremonial robes were conferred upon them.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十四年，巡撫胡來貢請改祀北嶽於渾源州。

translations.literal: In Wanli 14 the grand coordinator Hu Laigong requested changing the Northern Peak sacrifice to Hunyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 14 the grand coordinator Hu Laigong requested changing the Northern Peak sacrifice to Hunyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「《大明集禮》載，漢、唐、宋北嶽之祭，皆在定州曲陽縣，與史俱合。

translations.literal: Ritual officials said: "The Collected Rituals of the Great Ming records that Han, Tang, and Song sacrifices to the Northern Peak were all at Quyang County in Ding Prefecture, matching the histories throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials said: "The Collected Rituals of the Great Ming records that Han, Tang, and Song sacrifices to the Northern Peak were all at Quyang County in Ding Prefecture, matching the histories throughout.

sentences.zh: 渾源之稱北嶽，止見州志碑文，經傳無可考，仍祀曲陽是。」

translations.literal: Calling Hunyuan the Northern Peak appears only in the prefecture gazetteer and stele inscriptions; no verification exists in the classics and commentaries—Quyang should still be sacrificed to."
translations.idiomatic: Calling Hunyuan the Northern Peak appears only in the prefecture gazetteer and stele inscriptions; no verification exists in the classics and commentaries—Quyang should still be sacrificed to."

sentences.zh: 其他山川之祀。

translations.literal: Other mountains and rivers sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Other Mountains and Rivers Sacrifice
